items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Automated Detection and Segmentation of Pulp Stones in Cone Beam Computed Tomography Scans.
items.abstract: Objective : This study aimed to automatically detect the human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stones on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) using deep learning-based semantic segmentation. Methodology : 523 annotated images of teeth from 112 CBCT examinations were used to train and evaluate four established deep learning architectures (U-Net, Attention U-Net, U-Net++, and DeepLabV3+) in segmenting the background, pulp cavity, and pulp stone(s). Subsequently a novel architecture was developed (DACA-DeepLab) and evaluated through an additive study. DACA-DeepLab incorporates DeepLabV3+ with a pyramid channel-spatial attention (PCSA) module, a dual-axis cross-attention (DACA) decoder, and a Sobel-guided boundary-refinement (BFR) head. Results : DeepLabV3+ achieved the best overall Dice performance among the four baseline architectures (mean, 0.775; pulp cavity, 0.838; pulp stone, 0.711). In the second study, combining PCSA and DACA yielded the highest performance (mean Dice, 0.733). Adding the boundary-refinement head reduced performance, suggesting sensitivity to the limited training set. Conclusion : Deep learning-based semantic segmentation can accurately identify human tooth pulp cavity and pulp stone(s) on CBCT. These findings establish a systematic benchmark for CBCT-based pulp segmentation and provide a foundation for AI-assisted endodontic diagnosis and pre-treatment planning.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Middle and Secondary Education: Instructional Opportunities, Limitations and Ethical Considerations
items.abstract: Middle and secondary school educators should utilize and implement Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a support tool for instruction, not a replacement for their pedagogy and lesson planning. Utilizing and implementing AI can assist with lesson planning, differentiation, feedback, and generating learning materials; its uses should be guided by clear expectations, professional judgment, and school policy. Educators should also teach their students how to use AI ethically, verify outputs for accuracy and bias, and protect student privacy by avoiding sensitive data. Most importantly, assessments should be designed to show genuine student understanding, with AI used transparently and appropriately. The best available published advice concurs that the usage of AI within an educator’s pedagogy significantly enhances middle and secondary school students’ learning. This article offers practical guidance for educators who use or plan to use AI in the classroom, while also highlighting policy recommendations to support effective educational practices.

items.title: Assessment of Internal and External Occupational Exposure to NORM in the Brazilian Oil and Gas Industry
items.abstract: The Oil and Gas industry is one of twelve industries that can involve Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material (NORM), generating a considerable volume of waste in Brazil. The petroleum industry, NORM, is present in geological formations and is accumulated as a function of the process. The most important radionuclides found in scale and sludge are Radium-226 and Radium-228, with activity concentrations that can reach 3,500 Bq/g in the country. The management of NORMs, vital for the safety of workers and the population, as well as for minimizing environmental impacts, encompasses six stages: production and extraction, monitoring, cleaning and decontamination, radiological analysis of NORMs, transportation, and storage. In each phase, workers are exposed to radiological risks through external exposure (gamma radiation) and/or internal exposure (inhalation or ingestion of radioactive particles). Given the large volume of NORM (Naturally Occurring Radioactive Material) and the growing demand for decommissioning offshore platforms in Brazil, which involves handling these materials, the understanding and rigorous application of radiological protection protocols become crucial. Although regulations require occupational health services and individual monitoring, a gap exists in occupational radiological assessments for this sector in the country. Estimated effective doses for the ten workers were comparable and consistently below the LD (Detection Limit) throughout the period of routine NORM exposure. These values fluctuated according to the nature of the work performed. Results confirm that in vitro bioassay is a reliable monitoring method for the oil and gas industry, particularly when integrated with Hp(10) personal dosimetry and stringent safety protocols, ensuring comprehensive monitoring of occupationally exposed workers.

items.title: Auditing a Moving Target: Evidence Anchoring and the Expiry of Fairness Audits of Provider-Served Language Models
items.abstract: Organizations increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for decisions about people, such as hiring, investment and employee evaluation, and rely on them over long periods of time. Fairness audits of such systems, however, are conducted only once. We examine how the biases of LLMs change over time. In a venture screening setting, models from five providers decided whether and how much to invest in startups whose founders differed only in gender, origin and university. We repeated this audit three times over 13 months (248,400 API calls). Study 1 shows that the same model, called under the same identifier one year later, displayed a significantly different bias pattern. Study 2 shows that the successors of retired models carried the same bias as their predecessors, but in a significantly different size and form. Study 3 shows that the bias does not depend on the industry of the startup. A document analysis further shows that providers change and retire models at their discretion, with notice periods of zero to six months. Drawing on these findings, we develop a theory of evidence anchoring. We theorize that bias resides in the model class and persists, whereas audit evidence is anchored to a single model and expires when the provider decides. We derive policy advice for organizations and regulators, namely audits of model classes instead of single models, a version record for every model response, and re-audits triggered by model changes.

items.title: Augmenting Pretrained Language Models with N-gram Embeddings through Incremental Training
items.abstract: As a new scaling technique for large language models, the n-gram embedding improves the base ability of a model while adding almost no inference cost. Mainstream research realizes it through joint training of the n-gram embedding with the backbone, which severely restricts the settings in which an n-gram embedding can be used. We therefore propose training an n-gram embedding onto an existing model through incremental training, to extend where the technique can deliver value. Specifically, we explore several settings of the n-gram embedding under incremental training---the learning rate of the embedding, the vocabulary size, and the injection position---and train an n-gram embedding onto the existing model under the best configuration. Experiments show that the best configuration under incremental training does not fully coincide with that under pretraining; moreover, the incrementally trained knowledge is written predominantly into the n-gram embedding, while the general ability of the backbone is retained throughout this training process.

items.title: Automation, AI and the Changing Skills Demand for University Graduates: A Comparative Qualitative Study across Four Economic Sectors
items.abstract: Automation, digitalization, and, more recently, generative artificial intelligence (gAI) are changing the skill sets employers demand. However, understanding remains limited about how different sector-level stakeholders in developing countries perceive these innovations, and about these technologies' impact on university graduates' employability. The comparative qualitative study draws on 60 interviews with graduates, employer representatives and academics, five of each type per sector, in four Bangladeshi sectors (readymade garments and textiles (RMG); information and communication technology and IT-enabled services (ICT/ITES); banking and financial services; logistics and supply chain management), as well as multi-sector comparative data. Reflexive thematic analysis yielded cross-sector themes, which include framing of technology and specific discussion of AI in ICT/ITES, disciplinary expertise being necessary but no longer sufficient, with digital, data and adaptive capabilities increasingly essential and learned largely outside formal programmes, cross-sector problems with institutional coordination due to curricula lag (the mode and extent of lag varies according to discipline), reasons why these results should not be taken as an indication of job loss and the impact of gAI, as well as sector-specific and generic implications for universities, sectors and employer associations with clear links to the data. Shortcomings include reliance on perceptions, small cell sizes across multiple parameters, and a lack of a worker perspective.

items.title: Awareness, Perceptions, and Practices of Surgical Smoke Management: A Cross-Sectional Study Guided by Behavioral Reasoning Theory
items.abstract: Background Surgical smoke is an occupational health concern for operating theatre personnel because of repeated exposure to potentially hazardous substances. Despite available safety guidance, adherence to surgical smoke management practices remains inconsistent, and the behavioural factors influencing these practices are not well understood. This study aims to examine knowledge, awareness, perceptions, and practices from a behavioural perspective related to surgical smoke safety management among surgeons, anesthetists, and perioperative nurses in an acute hospital in Singapore. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among surgeons, anesthetists, and perioperative nurses who were recruited through convenience sampling. Participants voluntarily completed a validated online questionnaire guided by Westaby’s Behavioral Reasoning Theory. The questionnaire assessed demographics, awareness, perceptions and practices, and surgical smoke-related feedback. Results Among 80 participants, the mean general knowledge score was 1.91 ± 0.76. Most participants demonstrated moderate awareness (80.00%) and moderate perception and practice scores (77.50%). Awareness differed significantly by professional role (p < 0.001), with a significant interaction between professional role and general knowledge (p = 0.030). Nurses had significantly higher perception and practice scores than anesthetists and surgeons (p < 0.001). No significant association was found between awareness and perception and practice scores (p = 0.056). Conclusion The findings indicate persistent gaps in SS knowledge and inconsistent implementation of protective measures. A multifactorial approach combining standardized interdisciplinary education, practical training, engineering controls, and organizational policies is warranted to strengthen SS safety and protect surgical teams and patients from potential exposure.

items.title: Bajillion: Cryptographic Clearing for Micropayments
items.abstract: Much of the web is funded by advertising, a model that erodes as humans delegate browsing to AI agents acting on their behalf. A natural replacement is for agents to pay for what they consume, often a fraction of a cent per request. At the scale of web traffic, this could mean tens or even hundreds of millions of payments per second. We present Bajillion, a clearing protocol for scalable micropayments. A sender signs a payment request, and an untrusted operator answers with a preconfirmation, which promises the receiver that it will be paid. Periodically, the operator closes an epoch by posting only the net effect of its payments on chain. Bajillion guarantees that a malicious operator can only omit payments -- it can never debit a sender beyond what it signed, nor misdirect a transfer. Posted balances are therefore finalized immediately and can be withdrawn. By design, senders never have to raise disputes, making it suitable for ephemeral AI agents. A receiver that is shortchanged can prove that a close omitted a preconfirmed payment, which halts the protocol and lets every user exit with its finalized balance. Requests from different senders can be processed independently, allowing the operator to parallelize up to the number of senders. We capture these guarantees in an ideal functionality for accountable clearing and prove that Bajillion realizes it.

items.title: Benefits and Barriers to Human-AI Teaming for Crisis Counseling
items.abstract: Background: AI systems are increasingly deployed to support mental health clinicians, yet real-world evidence remains limited. In crisis counseling, where clients often seek human connection, understanding whether AI augmentation preserves or undermines meaningful human engagement is essential. Methods: In a mixed-methods study of a counselor-facing AI copilot on a WhatsApp-based crisis hotline in India (Mar.-Oct. 2025), counselors could request, edit, and send AI messages. We analyzed 20 interviews, 8 shadowing sessions, 56 survey responses, and edits in 27,778 copilot messages from 108 counselors via thematic analysis (Technology Acceptance Model 2, plus inductive coding of emergent factors), and survey statistics. Results: Counselors reported high copilot acceptance (survey): 98.2% found it helpful; 89.3% likely to continue use; 80.4% reported efficiency gains. Interviews highlighted sentence scaffolding, empathetic phrasing, stress reduction, catching missed details, and efficiency. Barriers (survey) included repetitive outputs (23.2%), lack of context (17.9%), and authenticity concerns (10.7%). While 69.6% (survey) reported skill enhancement, interviews surfaced skill atrophy concerns. Counselors frequently accepted copilot suggestions, editing to remove questions, adjust tone, or personalize style. Conclusion: In one of the largest real-world deployments of a counselor-facing mental health AI copilot, counselors reported reduced cognitive load, empathetic communication, and greater efficiency, alongside concerns about skill atrophy, authenticity, and over-reliance. In settings like crisis counseling where clients seek human connection, AI tools must balance operational support with preserving clinical skill and genuine therapeutic engagement. Designs soliciting approval or editing of complete drafts may overweight efficiency at the expense of sustained human engagement.

items.title: Better Questions or Better Questioning? Student-AI Co-Creation and Higher-Order Thinking in Transdisciplinary Engineering and Design Education
items.abstract: As higher education increasingly adopts transdisciplinary frameworks to address complex societal challenges, cultivating students’ higher-order thinking (HOT) skills has become a key educational goal. These cognitive processes are essential in Human Factors Engineering (HFE), which requires students to address wicked problems inherent in transdisciplinary human-technology systems. However, traditional HFE curricula often emphasise rote memorisation of scientific theories. Meanwhile, the widespread adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) has altered how students engage with academic content by enabling instant access to AI-generated responses. Despite increasing interest in AI-assisted learning, empirical evidence examining LLMs as co-creative partners in activities designed to support HOT remains limited. This quasi-experimental study compares two cohorts in an undergraduate HFE course, in which students either generated exam questions independently or co-created questions with an LLM. A total of 166 multiple-choice questions were collected and classified according to Bloom’s Taxonomy by two independent raters. Results indicate that the LLM-collaboration group produced a significantly higher proportion of higher-order questions. Among student-level factors, the number of student-AI dialogue turns was associated with question cognitive level, whereas self-reported AI usage frequency, metacognitive awareness and prior AI experience were not. Additionally, whether students adopted the AI’s suggested question or wrote their own after the dialogue did not affect question cognitive level. An exploratory analysis suggested that the number of turns in which students critically engaged with AI outputs was marginally associated with higher question cognitive level. These findings highlight the potential value of student-AI dialogue logs as a complementary source of assessment evidence.

items.title: Beyond Bilingual: Studying Quadrilingual Code-Switching with Conversational AI
items.abstract: Multilingual speakers choose languages by topic and conversation partner. Large language models (LLMs) support these languages unequally. Research on code-switching with conversational AI has mostly examined bilingual pairs of well-resourced languages. In Curaçao and Aruba, many people use Dutch, English, Spanish, and the low-resource Creole Papiamentu/o. In a preregistered study, 42 university students held two five-minute chatbot conversations, one about university life and one about local food and culture. Surveys assessed language background, AI use, and switching comfort. 20 international students in Curaçao formed a comparison sample. Participants switched between turns and rarely mixed languages within a message. English dominated both conversations. Participants switched more often in the cultural conversation, where Papiamentu/o and Spanish rose from 15% to 24% of messages. Self-reports showed no lower comfort switching with the chatbot than with a person. Conversational agents must follow turn-by-turn language changes and handle local low-resource languages well.

items.title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign
items.abstract: We introduce EJBench, a benchmark of engineering judgement: whether a model can predict how a design behaves at new conditions from a few earlier results, and decide on it. Unlike engineering benchmarks that test whether an agent can operate simulation or CAD software, EJBench is software-agnostic and asks what an engineer would conclude without running a simulation. Its tasks come from a conjugate heat transfer design campaign for battery cold plates, in three families: matching unlabelled test results to their operating points, choosing which stored runs to reveal before signing off a design, and ranking new duties by peak cell temperature. Every answer is taken from a converged simulation, not from an LLM judge. The best of ten frontier models, GPT-6 Astra, scores 0.71, and models state almost the same confidence on tasks they get wrong as on tasks they get right. We also post-train Qwen3.5-9B with LoRA and reinforcement learning, rewarded by the share of answer criteria the simulation results confirm; on the held-out test split its score rises from 0.071 to 0.106. We release the train, validation and test splits, the evaluation harness and the leaderboard.

items.title: Bridge-RoadLM: Building a Domain-Adapted Large Language Model for Bridge Pavement Maintenance Based on Authoritative Specification Corpora and Efficient Parameter Fine-Tuning
items.abstract: General large language models (LLMs) often have limited reliability when addressing specialized bridge pavement maintenance tasks. This study proposes Bridge-RoadLM, a domain-adapted framework for preliminary bridge pavement maintenance support. We developed an automated data engineering pipeline to construct the Bridge-Road Corpus, comprising 10,000 instruction-following samples derived from authoritative specifications and technical documents. Using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT/LoRA), representative Qwen, DeepSeek, LLaMA, and Gemma models were adapted to bridge pavement maintenance tasks. A multilevel evaluation framework was established, including automated linguistic metrics, a 500-question expert-validated test bank, and a blinded multiengineer evaluation of open-ended inspection-report-style cases. Results show improved controlled task performance for several fine-tuned models, and the strongest improvement was for Qwen3-8B. Its accuracy in pavement defect diagnosis increased from 45.0% to 81.0%, with 95% Wilson confidence intervals of 35.6%–54.8% and 72.2%–87.5%, respectively. Its accuracy in bridge monitoring and maintenance increased from 25.0% to 75.0%, with 95% Wilson confidence intervals of 17.5%–34.3% and 65.7%–82.5%, respectively. In the blinded open-ended evaluation, six engineers with 10–17 years of professional experience scored anonymized model outputs using five predefined criteria: correctness, completeness, traceability, hallucination control, and safety. Qwen3-8B achieved the highest average score among the nine evaluated models. The results also show that fine-tuning effects varied across model families, indicating that domain-specific PEFT does not uniformly improve all LLMs. Overall, this study provides a specification-based instruction corpus and a controlled evaluation workflow for adapting locally deployable LLMs to bridge pavement maintenance, supporting preliminary specification referencing, defect interpretation, and draft-level maintenance-plan preparation within a human-in-the-loop workflow.

items.abstract: OFFICIAL DESCRIPTION OF THE SCIENTIFIC WORK | INTERNATIONAL CATALOG 2026 RESEARCH TITLE: BUILD OR DESTROY: A CRITICAL ANALYSIS OF THE TRANSFORMATIVE POTENTIAL AND DISINFORMATION RISKS OF MODERN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE LEAD RESEARCHER: Dr. Dieudelin Arcangel Legrand - Brotherswagg Robert Academic Jurisdiction and Country of Origin: Republic of Haiti PRIMARY PUBLISHING HOUSE: BrotherswaggStudioRecords Publishing (BSR Publishing) / TM3 MUSIC GROUP INSTITUTIONAL CORPORATE AUTHORSHIP, APPROVAL AND EDITORIAL REVIEW ENDORSEMENT: International Institutional Academic Editorial Committee (IIAEC) and its International Research Consortium: - The Hellenic Institute (Critical Thinking and Theoretical Frameworks) - The Atlantic Research Group (Factual Analysis and Global Perspective) - The Euro-Academic Council (Literary Standards and European Editorial Review) - The Oxbridge Academic (Methodological Rigor and Technical Review) - The Continental Bureau (Source Documentation and Multilingual Research) INTERNATIONAL EDITION: November 2026 ORIGINAL LANGUAGE OF PUBLICATION: Spanish (Official Master Edition) --- 1. SCIENTIFIC CLASSIFICATION AND EPISTEMOLOGICAL NATURE OF THE WORK This publication belongs to the genre of the Critical Review Scientific Article, Epistemological Analysis, and Technological Foresight (an In-Depth Argumentative Scientific Essay). By virtue of its interdisciplinary structure, the work is classified within the fields of Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, and Philosophy of Technology, while establishing direct analytical connections with Communication Studies, Digital Sociology, Applied Ethics, Cognitive Psychology of Perception, and Cyber Law. Having undergone a rigorous process of methodological auditing and structural verification under the standards of the International Institutional Academic Editorial Committee (IIAEC), this research distinguishes itself from conventional technical literature through its comprehensive scope and unwavering commitment to empirical truth. It is neither a merely descriptive manual nor a speculative pamphlet, but rather a reference work designed to diagnose, with surgical precision, the most consequential technological phenomenon of our time. 2. WHY THIS WORK IS ESSENTIAL READING IN THE 21ST CENTURY Humanity is experiencing a historic moment in which the boundary between the real and the artificial has been erased by the speed of algorithms. Every day, millions of people interact with texts, voices, photographs, and video sequences that appear to reflect authentic events but have actually been entirely fabricated by generative artificial intelligence systems. Faced with this unprecedented reality, global society oscillates between two equally dangerous extremes: naïve fascination with the power of machines and uninformed panic in the face of a technology that few people fully understand. "Build or Destroy: A Critical Analysis of the Transformative Potential and Disinformation Risks of Modern Artificial Intelligence" was conceived to dispel this conceptual fog. This work confronts readers with an unavoidable question: How is it possible that the same technology capable of saving lives in medicine, accelerating scientific discoveries, and democratizing education has simultaneously become the preferred tool of countless digital content creators for falsifying reality, impersonating identities, and monetizing deception on a planetary scale? Through rigorous, direct, transparent prose, free from corporate constraints, the Lead Researcher, Dr. Dieudelin Arcangel Legrand - Brotherswagg Robert, together with the IIAEC collegiate body and BSR Publishing, exposes the hidden mechanisms behind this duality without barriers or concealment. Readers who explore these pages will encounter documented truths about how the attention economy operates, why digital platforms amplify synthetic falsehoods, and how society can defend its right to truth without renouncing scientific progress. 3. THE ARCHITECTURE OF THE WORK: AN EVOLUTIONARY NARRATIVE IN FOUR FOUNDATIONAL MODULES To provide a progressive, logical, and deeply enriching reading experience, this research has been structured into seven sections organized around four foundational modules that evolve as one continuous scientific narrative: - FIRST FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | Recent Evolution and Future Horizons of AI: Guides readers from the origins of symbolic computing to the transformer revolution, multimodal foundation models, and emerging autonomous agentic systems, clearly explaining how machines acquired the ability to synthesize realities indistinguishable from the physical world. - SECOND FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | The Constructive and Transformative Potential: Rigorously documents the positive side of this revolution, demonstrating how artificial intelligence is transforming medical diagnosis, drug design, climate sustainability, space research, the inclusion of persons with disabilities, and the democratization of knowledge in every corner of the planet. - THIRD FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | The Anatomy of Deception and a Critical Examination of Malicious Use: Constitutes the critical and revealing core of the manuscript. It examines with intellectual courage how numerous unscrupulous content creators exploit AI to manufacture deepfakes, clone human voices, fabricate pseudo-scientific or pseudo-journalistic evidence, and operate artificial engagement farms, thereby undermining the historical principle of audiovisual evidence and profiting from public credulity. - FOURTH FOUNDATIONAL MODULE | Ethical Discussion, Governance, and the Future of Trust: Proposes concrete solutions to the epistemic crisis by establishing the principles of mandatory transparency, cryptographic traceability from the point of origin, the legal shared responsibility of digital platforms, and the urgent need for critical literacy among citizens. 4. RELEVANCE TO UNIVERSITIES, RESEARCHERS, STUDENTS, AND SOCIETY This work has been conceived as an indispensable reference resource for multiple sectors of the global community: - For Researchers and Academics: It offers an interdisciplinary theoretical framework integrating algorithmic engineering, epistemology, and digital sociology, supported by cutting-edge technical references and international standards. - For Universities and Academic Institutions: It constitutes a bibliographic resource of significant educational value for courses in technological ethics, social communication, computer science, digital law, and contemporary philosophy. - For Students and Young Creators: It provides a moral and technical compass for understanding the power of the tools at their disposal, inspiring them to use artificial intelligence to build genuine knowledge and reject the culture of digital fraud. - For Citizens, Journalists, and the General Public: It delivers the practical and conceptual tools necessary to protect independent judgment against media manipulation and distinguish genuine progress from synthetic illusion. 5. A UNIVERSAL INVITATION: A WORK FOR EVERYONE, BREAKING DOWN BARRIERS AND BUILDING KNOWLEDGE WITHOUT BORDERS Beyond its methodological rigor and technical soundness, this research carries a fundamental declaration of principles: genuine scientific knowledge does not belong to closed elites or intellectual monopolies; it belongs to all humanity. For far too long, the production and validation of global knowledge have been concentrated within hermetic academic canons that erected invisible barriers—geographical, economic, linguistic, and racial—to determine who had the right to conduct research, publish, and be heard. Conceived in the Republic of Haiti with a global outlook and supported by the alliance between BrotherswaggStudioRecords Publishing (BSR Publishing) / TM3 MUSIC GROUP and the International Institutional Academic Editorial Committee (IIAEC), this work deliberately breaks through these historical barriers. It demonstrates that cutting-edge critical thinking, scientific excellence, and the ethical defense of truth can and must emerge from the Global South and reach the entire world, engaging in dialogue on equal terms with institutions across every nation. For this reason, an open, fraternal, and universal invitation is extended to all readers, students, professors, universities, independent researchers, artists, journalists, and citizens of every nation, origin, and circumstance: this work belongs to you. Every page of this study contains essential truths for understanding the world in which we live and defending the future we share. The entire global community is invited to read this article with a critical mindset, debate its arguments in classrooms and across digital networks, cite its findings, translate its message, and actively contribute to the development of an open, inclusive body of scientific literature, free from intellectual racism and committed to human dignity. Because only when knowledge is freed from chains and shared without exclusion does science fulfill its noblest purpose: to illuminate the minds of all human beings. items.title: Can Coding Agents Write and Transpile Unit Tests
items.abstract: Coding assistants built on Large Language Models (LLMs) have become a staple of modern software development, increasingly trusted to execute workflows and modernize code end-to-end. Much of this trust rests on passing tests, which are often written by the coding agents themselves. In this work, we examine the ability of these agents to both write reliable tests and translate them between programming languages. We benchmark three popular coding agents, each evaluated with a native frontier model and high reasoning effort. Verifying across a broad suite of metrics, we find that coding agents far exceed human written suites on traditional measures of coverage. This advantage, however, is uneven: agent test quality degrades sharply with project size, and much of the advantage lies in a greater number of written tests. We also show that agentic test translation---while seemingly strong in aggregate---remains inconsistent and unreliable.

items.title: CARDIO-ML-ED Dataset: A Multi-modal Clinical ECG Database for Machine Learning Applications and Data Analysis
items.abstract: Objectives: The CARDIO-ML-ED dataset was collected to address the critical shortage of publicly available cardiovascular databases that integrate electrocardiogram (ECG) imagery with comprehensive clinical metadata. Existing ECG repositories lack detailed patient-level information such as laboratory results, vital signs, and medical history—factors essential for developing clinically meaningful machine learning models. We aimed to create a curated, well-labelled, multimodal resource that supports research in automated ECG interpretation, multimodal fusion, and exploratory clinical phenotyping, while promoting reproducibility and innovation in artificial intelligence (AI) driven cardiovascular care. Data description: The CARDIO-ML-ED dataset comprises two complementary components: (1) structured clinical metadata for 582 subjects, and (2) a curated subset of 408 high-resolution ECG images derived from paper-based records digitized through standardized scanning, normalization, cropping, quality filtering, and noise reduction. The dataset includes 82 clinical features per subject—covering demographics, vital signs, laboratory tests (complete blood count, cardiac enzymes, electrolytes, inflammatory markers, arterial blood gases), and medical history. Diagnostic labels were independently assigned by a cardiologist and an emergency medicine physician, achieving substantial interrater agreement (Cohen's kappa = 0.82). This resource offers unique value through its dense integration of ECG data with clinical covariates, enabling multimodal fusion research, unsupervised clustering, imbalanced learning, and predictive analytics.

items.title: Catalysing system reforms in Pakistan’s Healthcare and Health Professions Education: National Stakeholder priorities for strengthening policy and system Governance
items.abstract: Objective Pakistan has broadened its medical and dental education sphere, yet apprehensions last about undergraduates’ competence, impact of regulation, international acknowledgment of qualifications and retention of the health workforce. This study explored multi stakeholder perspectives on training capacity, quality of education, governance, regulation and acknowledgment of health professions education in Pakistan, and identified prime reforms. Methodology: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted using hybrid focus group discussion held on 4 August 2026 as part of national Health and Education Summit Pakistan (HESP) 2026. Fourteen purposively sampled stakeholders participated in discussion guided by 16 semi structured questions. Data were analysed using Framework Method, and Health Policy Triangle was applied as an interpretive lens. Results Nine themes were identified across three domains. Educational quality and competence : undefined and unenforced competency standards; deficits in clinical training infrastructure; faculty development and continuous quality improvement; and cautious, purpose-specific integration of artificial intelligence. Governance, regulation and recognition : fragmented, input-oriented governance; private-sector representation and public–private imbalance; and international recognition and global alignment. Workforce and equity : equity in workforce planning; and workforce sustainability, security and dignity. Participants identified main barrier to reform is not in an absence of policy but in weak implementation, input based accreditation and poor coordination among regulatory bodies. Conclusion Stakeholders called for a shift from input based to outcome-based accreditation built on a nationally agreed definition of competence, a shared inter agency governance platform, documented clinical supervision and simulation, and workforce protection measures.

items.title: Characterisation of Air Quality and Respiratory Health Risks: A Management Framework for a Nigerian Aviation Hub
items.abstract: Airport operational environments generate complex emission matrices that pose severe occupational health hazards, particularly in developing nations lacking systematic surveillance frameworks. This study characterised air quality dynamics at Benin City Airport, Nigeria, and evaluated the associated respiratory health burden among personnel. A cross-sectional mixed-methods design was deployed, combining eight weeks of real-time microenvironmental monitoring (CO₂, PM₁₀, PM₂.₅) with an epidemiological survey across 129 eligible airport workers. Significant spatiotemporal variations were detected for particulate matter: the airside zone exhibited peak coarse particle concentrations (PM₁₀: 22.04 ± 0.94 µg/m³) during morning shifts and progressive fine particle accumulation (PM₂.₅) during afternoon shifts, tracking flight operational cycles. Gaseous CO₂ concentrations showed no significant spatial variations across monitoring sites. Respiratory symptom prevalence was high among workers, dominated by chronic cough (57.4%) and shortness of breath (24.0%). Multivariable logistic regression revealed an exposure-awareness paradox: personnel in high-exposure operational zones (Airside and Terminal Halls) experienced significantly higher respiratory morbidity despite reporting higher occupational safety knowledge. Unawareness of safe exposure limits was inversely associated with chronic cough (AOR = 0.38, p = 0.032). High and fluctuating particulate levels create continuous inhalation hazards for frontline personnel. Mitigating these chronic occupational risks requires optimising administrative controls, enforcing mandatory shift rotations, ensuring consistent personal protective equipment (PPE) compliance, and establishing routine environmental health surveillance frameworks.

items.title: CliniCIRCA: LLM-powered Clinical Timeline Generation and Summarization from Unstructured EHR Texts for Mental Health Patients
items.abstract: Background: Mental health care often requires clinicians to reason over patient journeys: longitudinal patterns of symptoms, diagnoses, treatments, behaviors, social context, and responses to care. Yet these journeys are rarely documented as readily available, explicit timelines. Clinically important temporal information is often embedded in unstructured discharge narratives, where events may be repeated, narrated out of order, or expressed through vague and relative time references. This makes temporal recovery difficult for clinicians and computational systems, and can limit the reliability of downstream summarization. Methods: We present CliniCIRCA, a multi-stage large language model (LLM) framework for Calendar-anchored, Imprecision-aware Reconstruction of Clinical Annals. CliniCIRCA decomposes patient-journey reconstruction into three stages: extracting atomic clinical events from raw discharge summaries, assigning calendar-grounded temporal labels with explicit uncertainty, and rendering the verified timeline as a date-grouped clinical summary. The framework is designed to make temporal reasoning inspectable rather than hidden inside a single summarization step. Results: From 14,882 MIMIC-III mental-health-coded admissions, we construct a benchmark of 52 discharge summaries on which CliniCIRCA produces 15,891 temporally tagged events. Following clinician-defined rubrics, human annotation with clinician adjudication corrects 629 errors, producing verified gold-standard timelines. These corrected timelines then drive a temporally grounded summarization stage that compresses each source 1.52 times into a date-grouped chronological record while preserving temporal labels and uncertainty. We further scale the framework to generate 1,000 silver-standard timelines and evaluate them as supervision for smaller open-weight models. Compared with zero- and few-shot prompting, instruction tuning generally improves five open-weight models across event extraction, temporal tagging, and summarization under both silver and clinician-verified evaluations. Conclusions: Auditable temporal reconstruction can serve as both a clinician-readable representation of complex mental health narratives and a reusable supervision source for smaller models. These findings suggest that intermediate, temporally grounded representations may help bridge clinical summarization, timeline generation, and scalable model adaptation, while preserving the need for expert adjudication in high-stakes clinical natural language processing (NLP).

items.title: COA-Tuning: Collaborative Adapter Tuning with Prompt Enhancement for Class-Incremental Medical Image Learning
items.abstract: Continual learning plays a crucial role in enabling artificial intelligence systems to accumulate knowledge over time without overwriting previously acquired information. While this capability is essential for real-world applications, especially in clinical domains where data evolves continuously, most existing approaches are designed for natural image scenarios and struggle when applied to medical imaging tasks. Medical images exhibit high intra-class similarity, making fine-grained recognition difficult. Meanwhile, adapter-based tuning with pretrained Vision Transformers introduces task-agnostic inference challenges due to the lack of task identity at test time. To overcome these obstacles, we propose a continual learning framework tailored for medical imaging, which enhances training and inference in class-incremental settings. First, we introduce a prompt-guided adapter design that focuses the model’s representation capacity on subtle disease-specific differences, improving feature discrimination. Second, we encourage knowledge reuse by facilitating communication between task-specific adapters, allowing the model to build upon prior information. Finally, during testing, we employ a collaborative inference mechanism that dynamically integrates multiple adapters, enabling robust predictions without relying on task labels. Experiments on several public medical image datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance and substantially alleviates forgetting compared to existing methods.

items.title: CompCert4Lean: Porting a Verified C Compiler to Lean in Six Weeks with Parallel Coding Agents
items.abstract: We present CompCert4Lean, a large-scale port of CompCert 3.17's verified compiler core from Rocq to Lean, completed in approximately six weeks by one expert directing parallel LLM agents. Our migration workflow partitions the development along its dependencies, audits translated definitions and theorem statements before large-scale proof reconstruction, and then reconstructs proofs in parallel against stable interfaces. The resulting compiler covers typed CompCert C through x86-64 assembly, discharges all 4,908 recorded proof obligations without project-specific axioms, and produces executable Linux binaries. The workflow enabled the expert to concentrate on organizing the work rather than supplying technical solutions. Of 1,071 human interactions, 88.8% concerned workflow and coordination, while only three supplied technical direction. Optimization campaigns further demonstrate the benefit of the Lean port for agent-driven verified development. Under matched budgets of 24 active hours, GPT-6-astra produced a Lean candidate with 11.7% lower generated-program runtime across 29 small-tests programs, compared with 2.3% lower for its Rocq candidate, both relative to original CompCert 3.17 and while preserving the end-to-end correctness theorem. These results show that parallel LLM agents can support large-scale migration with limited human technical direction and subsequently improve the migrated compiler while retaining its formal guarantees.

items.title: Contrastive Activation-Guided Zeroth-Order Preference Optimisation for Memory-Efficient LLM Alignment
items.abstract: Direct Preference Optimisation (DPO) simplifies reinforcement learning from human feedback, but still relies on traditional backpropagation and its associated activation-memory cost. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimisation avoids backpropagation, yet isotropic perturbations can produce noisy updates for preference objectives defined by differences between chosen and rejected responses. We introduce Contrastive Activation-guided Zeroth-Order Direct Preference Optimisation (CA-ZODPO), which constructs a low-rank search subspace from the activation discrepancy between the chosen and rejected responses in each preference pair. Perturbations are restricted to this subspace, while momentum is maintained in low-rank coordinates to preserve the memory advantages of ZO training. On Qwen2.5-1.5B with Anthropic HH-RLHF, CA-ZODPO outperforms common ZO baselines and remains competitive with first-order DPO in pairwise preference evaluation. It also reduces peak GPU memory by about 59\% at a sequence length of 2048 while retaining the sequence-length scaling behaviour of zeroth-order training.

items.title: ControlAR: Contrasting Smartphone Text Entry and Trackpad Pointing for Head-Mounted Augmented Reality
items.abstract: Smartphones have repeatedly been proposed as companion input devices for head-mounted augmented reality (AR), but their usefulness depends on how the phone’s native interaction properties map onto the AR task. We present ControlAR, a prototype connecting an iPhone to a Magic Leap One through Bluetooth Low Energy and contrast two deliberately different mappings: direct text entry using the standard iOS keyboard and indirect spatial selection using a relative touchscreen trackpad. In a within-subject study with 18 participants, both mappings were compared with the Magic Leap One controller. Smartphone text entry was substantially faster (65.42 vs. 221.37 s), more accurate (0.73% vs. 2.18% errors), and rated more usable (SUS 92.08 vs. 71.67). For pointer selection, the smartphone was faster overall (68.43 vs. 76.68 s), yet the Magic Leap controller received markedly higher usability ratings (SUS 88.89 vs. 65.97). Rather than proposing a new pointing metaphor, we empirically characterize two pragmatic smartphone-to-AR mappings: direct reuse of mature touchscreen input and repurposing touch as relative spatial control. The results expose a speed–usability dissociation for trackpad pointing and identify tactile confirmation, ergonomics, and pointer gain as concrete design concerns.

items.title: CP-Agent: A harness-engineered agent for crystal plasticity simulation workflows
items.abstract: Crystal plasticity (CP) simulations are widely used to predict the mechanical behavior of polycrystalline metals, yet their routine application remains hindered by the substantial manual effort of configuring heterogeneous tools, orchestrating multi-step data pipelines, and calibrating constitutive parameters against experimental measurements. These bottlenecks impede productivity in systematic parameter studies, motivating growing interest in automated workflow solutions. This study presents CP-Agent , a harness-engineered LLM-based agent that autonomously executes complete CP modeling workflows from tasks specified in natural language. Operating under the ReAct paradigm, the agent reasons about tool selection and sequencing while delegating numerical search to established optimizers. The harness comprises a minimal system prompt, typed tool definitions, a dispatcher, and a safety-bounded iteration loop, encoding domain knowledge through tool schemas rather than hard-coded logic. CP-Agent is demonstrated on four case studies: calibrating four slip parameters of additively manufactured stainless steel 316L against tensile data; validating the workflow against published copper benchmarks, reproducing stress–strain and texture evolution; recovering the initial crystallographic texture of copper, where the agent correctly identifies a diffuse initial texture; and reproducing the multi-pass rolling texture evolution of a Mg-Zn-Ca alloy, where the agent chains five deformation passes and recovers the experimentally observed weakened, split basal texture. In all cases, the agent inferred the correct execution sequence from the task statement, robustly across repeated runs, and delivered physically interpretable results. This work establishes harness engineering as a systematic approach to automating CP modeling workflows while maintaining physical interpretability and auditability through visible reasoning traces.

items.title: Cross-Domain Transfer of Depression Voice Biomarkers Depends on the Outcome Instrument: Leakage-Controlled Cross-Sectional Evaluation Study
items.abstract: Background Voice-based depression screening is commercializing rapidly, yet whether voice biomarkers generalize across clinical settings is largely untested. Generalization is usually framed as a question about populations, but it is also a question about the outcome instrument a model is scored against, an effect confounded with other between-study differences in the literature. Objective We tested whether depression voice biomarkers transfer between perinatal and general-psychiatric speech in both directions under strict leakage control and whether transfer depends on the screening instrument. Methods In a cross-sectional, online US study, 390 pregnant participants at a mean of 22 (SD 1) weeks’ gestation (analytical sample n=316) participated in 446 sessions; each participant provided 4 voice recordings and completed the modified 8-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-8) and modified 9-item Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (mEPDS-9). We extracted 375 acoustic descriptors and 330-dimensional Population Dynamics Foundation Model community-health embeddings. Discrimination area under the curve (AUC) was assessed under leakage-controlled cross-validation, with feature and classifier selection inside training folds only and a permutation negative-control harness, across a prespecified grid of 4 speech tasks×4 outcome definitions. The prenatal-trained model was applied to 2 general-psychiatric corpora (Distress Analysis Interview Corpus–Wizard-of-Oz, n=189; Extended Distress Analysis Interview Corpus, n=219) under pure held-out inference, and the open-source Kintsugi Depression/Anxiety Model (DAM), trained on 35,000 individuals, was applied to all 3 cohorts without refitting, with Benjamini-Hochberg multiplicity control. Results In the prenatal cohort, the preregistered outcome was at chance (AUC 0.494, 95% CI 0.431-0.560); no cell in the 16-cell grid survived adjustment under either modeling paradigm. The prenatal-trained model did not transfer to either general-psychiatric corpus (AUCs 0.505 and 0.478). Reverse transfer depended on the screening instrument. The DAM reached an AUC of 0.706 to 0.708 on general-psychiatric speech. In the same participants, it performed at chance against the PHQ-8 (AUC 0.510, 95% CI 0.411-0.609) but discriminated against the mEPDS-9 (AUC 0.645, 95% CI 0.541-0.744), a paired difference of 0.135 (95% CI 0.019-0.248; unadjusted post hoc P =0.02). Exploratory item-level analysis suggests a mechanism: the DAM tracked affective-distress items (crying r =0.26, sadness r =0.21, and overwhelmed r =0.20) but not somatic PHQ-8 items; only crying survived adjustment across 17 tests. Transfer varied by elicitation task (pregnancy narrative 0.653, 95% CI 0.550-0.753; open-ended speech 0.597, 95% CI 0.486-0.699; scripted reading 0.544, 95% CI 0.434-0.651), though these were not formally compared. Conclusions Cross-domain comparison showed a compound shift: population, elicitation task, and outcome instrument differed together, while only the instrument could be varied on its own. Whether a depression voice biomarker transfers may depend not only on the population but also on whether the outcome instrument captures what the model can detect. Validation should state the population, elicitation task, and outcome instrument together; a tool validated against one instrument should not be assumed to work against another.

items.title: Curriculum-aligned analysis of assessment feedback: a retrieval-augmented large language model approach for revealing fine-grained student error patterns in higher education
items.abstract: Assessment feedback in higher education provides fine-grained evidence about students’ specific errors but remains underutilized as a data source for teaching improvement. This study proposes a method based on a large language model (LLM) that transforms unstructured feedback into curriculum-aligned error analysis in three steps, deriving an error taxonomy from the feedback, mapping each piece to curriculum content by retrieval-augmented generation, and aggregating the annotations into error patterns with quantified cohort coverage. The method was applied to 6072 pieces of feedback across four cohorts (2022–2025) of an undergraduate engineering course. The feedback resolved into recurring, curriculum-aligned error patterns, dominated by missing content and justification, clustered in identifiable modules and weeks, and more than half recurring across cohorts. The resulting annotations achieved 89.1% agreement with human judgment, substantially higher than the 74.7% obtained when an expert-designed taxonomy was applied to the same data. In a focus group, the teaching team confirmed the patterns against their marking experience, proposed course revisions from them, and set the bound that they serve as a reference and not as a direct measure of teaching quality. The study reports a process account of this team’s use of curriculum-aligned error analytics, built on sensemaking and pedagogical response. The analysis turns feedback written for students into evidence on the teaching that preceded it, by which a teaching team can check the alignment between intended outcomes, teaching, and assessment in students’ actual work, reflect on its own practice, and improve its teaching across cohorts.

items.title: Deep Learning for Physicists: From Linear Regression to Reasoning Models
items.abstract: These lecture notes are based on an introductory course on neural networks and deep learning that the author taught in the School of Mathematical Sciences at Queen Mary University of London in 2023/24 and 2024/25. The author, however, is a physicist, and it shows: wherever possible, ideas are explained with physical intuition rather than heavy formalism. Readers with a background in physics or mathematics who want a self-contained, introductory route into modern machine learning may therefore find these notes particularly friendly. The notes start from maximum likelihood, least squares, linear regression and (stochastic) gradient descent. They then cover neural networks, backpropagation, the vanishing gradient problem, batch and layer normalization, overfitting and regularization, adversarial examples, and the kernel method. The second half turns to natural language processing: word embeddings, recurrent networks and LSTMs, the attention mechanism and Transformers, and large language models, including scaling laws, the history of GPT, instruction tuning, reinforcement learning from human feedback, hallucination, alignment faking, chain-of-thought reasoning and test-time scaling. The emphasis on large language models reflects requests from the students. The notes are aimed at third- and fourth-year students in the UK system. Because the course was also taken by students from other departments, very little is assumed: even basic material such as matrix multiplication is explained from scratch, so readers familiar with it can safely skip such parts. No originality is claimed; the aim is a coherent, intuitive path through the material. Developments after spring 2025 are not covered, but the basic ideas emphasized here are unlikely to go out of date soon.

items.title: Deploying a Control-Logic LLM Assistant in Air-Gapped Power Plants: Lessons in Source Authority and Bounded Retrieval
items.abstract: Deploying Large Language Model (LLM) assistants in industrial operational technology environments poses constraints largely absent from cloud applications: site policies restrict engineering and operational data from leaving the plant, on-premises compute is limited, and incorrect causal attribution can mislead incident response. We report lessons from deploying a control-logic evidence layer that underpins a broader on-premises operator assistance system at two gas power plants. Two prototypes revealed where generative models added avoidable uncertainty and cost. The first used a Vision Language Model (VLM) to reconstruct control topology from PDF printouts routinely exchanged by engineers. Across the full 6,979-page document, extraction reached 0.51 connection precision and required 3.1 hours on 4xH200 GPUs; consultation with controls engineers then revealed a native structured export from the authoring system. The second used an LLM tool-calling agent to plan repeatedly over eight predefined graph operations. In a controlled benchmark of 40 template-generated questions, replacing this agent with explicit execution plans reduced mean token use by 20x and median latency by 3x, with identical retrieved node sets across repeated runs. The deployed design ingests the authoritative export into a versioned knowledge graph, executes bounded graph operations in fixed software, and confines the local LLM to fallback intent classification and evidence-grounded explanation. At one site, the graph contains 221K nodes across seven controllers. Our experience suggests a practical division of labor for high-consequence AI: LLMs interpret natural-language requests and explain results, while deterministic software constructs and retrieves technical evidence grounded in authoritative sources. Abstention, entity disambiguation, graph versioning, and read-only integration provide additional safeguards.

However, existing disposal incinerators operated by state authorities, such as Jabatan Agama Islam Melaka (JAIM), face significant operational issues, including excessive toxic smoke emissions, ergonomic limitations, ash loss due to wind scattering, and performance degradation from 300 kg/day to 150 kg/day after two years. items.title: Designing Cognitive Scaffolds for Generative-AI-Assisted Introductory Programming
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can make introductory programming tasks easier to complete, but a working program is not evidence of durable learning. This conceptual-theoretical paper integrates research on cognitive load, metacognition, self-explanation, productive failure, appropriate reliance on automation, and recent studies of AI-assisted programming to propose a five-phase cognitive-scaffolding framework. Learners first make an unaided attempt, request bounded assistance, verify the response against requirements and independently designed tests, explain the mechanism and calibrate confidence, and then complete a related transfer task as support fades. AI literacy, ethical disclosure, privacy, and instructor orchestration operate across all phases. The framework identifies process evidence that remains inspectable when generated code is available, including problem representations, hypotheses, verification records, explanations, confidence judgments, and unaided transfer. It also states six testable propositions and an evaluation blueprint for introductory programming courses. The contribution is a bounded design logic, not a claim that the sequence has already been validated: GenAI should reduce avoidable burden while leaving consequential decisions, checks, and explanations with the learner.

items.title: Designing metacognitive scaffolding in flipped learning to enhance students’ visual–spatial reasoning: Evidence from geometry instruction
items.abstract: The development of students’ visual–spatial reasoning is a persistent challenge in geometry learning, where abstract representations and spatial transformations require high levels of cognitive engagement. Although flipped learning has been widely implemented to promote active learning, its effectiveness largely depends on the quality of instructional design and pedagogical support provided during in-class activities. This study investigates how metacognitive scaffolding can be intentionally designed and embedded within flipped learning to enhance students’ visual–spatial reasoning. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design was employed in secondary geometry instruction involving 62 students assigned to experimental and control groups. Quantitative data were collected through pre- and post-tests of visual–spatial reasoning, while qualitative data were obtained from classroom observations and semi-structured teacher interviews. The results indicate that students who experienced metacognitive scaffolding within a flipped learning environment demonstrated significantly greater gains in visual–spatial reasoning than those in a conventional flipped classroom, with a large effect size. Qualitative findings further reveal that scaffolding prompts supported students’ planning, monitoring, and reflective evaluation during problem-solving activities. Overall, the findings suggest that flipped learning environments become more cognitively productive when structured metacognitive scaffolding is deliberately incorporated into the learning design.

items.title: Development and User-Centred Evaluation of a 3D-Printed Assistive Tool for Vehicle Fuel Cap Opening
items.abstract: Opening a vehicle fuel cap can be challenging for individuals experiencing reduced hand strength, impaired motor control, or upper-limb functional limitations because the task requires secure gripping and rotational force. This preliminary study aimed to develop and evaluate 3D-printed assistive-tool concepts for vehicle fuel-cap manipulation using a user-centred approach involving end users and occupational therapy (OT) professionals. Four initial design concepts were developed, of which two prototypes were selected for user evaluation. The prototypes were demonstrated with support from the Rehabilitation Department of Hospital Taiping and evaluated using a structured five-point Likert-scale instrument. Eleven end-user respondents and four OT professionals participated in the evaluation. End users assessed ease of use, ergonomics, effectiveness, safety, and user satisfaction, while OT professionals assessed clinical suitability, ergonomics, safety, functional benefit, and potential for practical application. The end-user group produced overall mean scores of 3.96 for Design 1 and 4.04 for Design 2, indicating generally favourable perceptions of both prototypes and a marginally higher rating for Design 2. OT professionals provided a higher overall rating for Design 1 (5.00) than Design 2 (3.63). Qualitative feedback highlighted the need for improved hand support, grip security, handle configuration, and fuel-cap engagement. The differing evaluations between end users and OT professionals suggest that stakeholder perspectives should be considered concurrently during early-stage assistive-device development. The findings support the feasibility of using 3D printing to rapidly develop task-specific assistive-tool prototypes, while the current results should be interpreted as preliminary rather than evidence of clinical effectiveness. Future work should incorporate objective measurements of grip force, rotational torque, task completion time, mechanical durability, and compatibility with different fuel-cap geometries.

items.title: Development of a Modular, Wheelchair-Accessible Desk Using Design Thinking and User-Centered Design (UCD).
items.abstract: Conventional desks are designed around fixed dimensions and lower structural elements that can hinder frontal approach, reach, and comfortable posture for wheelchair users, limiting their participation in study and work activities. This study aimed to develop a modular and accessible desk concept for wheelchair users through Design Thinking and User-Centered Design. An applied, mixed-methods, descriptive-propositive approach was followed, structured in the five phases of Design Thinking: empathize, define, ideate, prototype, and test. In the empathize phase, a questionnaire with two five-point Likert scales (perceived difficulty and importance of desk features) was administered to ten people, six wheelchair users and four non-users, selected through non-probability sampling. Data were analyzed descriptively, and internal consistency was estimated with Cronbach’s alpha. Both scales showed high internal consistency (α = 0.955 and 0.929). The greatest difficulties were plugging in devices and maintaining posture during long periods, while height adjustment, removable storage modules, and ample work surface were the most valued features (mean = 4.20). These findings informed a design brief, a conceptual sketch, and a three-dimensional model of an L-shaped desk with adjustable height, removable storage modules, device charging, and open space for frontal approach. The project is currently at the three-dimensional modeling stage; a physical prototype has not been built, and usability, stability, and ergonomic tests with users remain pending. Because of the small sample and the preliminary nature of the instrument, the results are exploratory and support the relevance of the proposed features rather than confirming the effectiveness of the desk. Future work will build the prototype and evaluate it with a larger group of wheelchair users.

items.title: Development of an HPLC Analytical Method Based on Large Language Models:A Case Study of the Eczema External Wash Formula
items.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) formulas feature complex chemical compositions, and their HPLC quality control method development is time-consuming and experience-dependent. Large language models (LLMs) provide a promising strategy for intelligently assisting analytical method construction. Taking the Eczema External Wash Formula as the research object, this work constructed a human-machine collaborative workflow involving intelligent recommendation, experimental validation and iterative optimization for HPLC method development. Among five prompt strategies tested, expert-role setting with structured reasoning performed best. After inputting formula information, the LLM proposed five chromatographic schemes. Through experimental screening and optimization, the final HPLC method used a SunShell C18 column, mobile phase of 0.1% aqueous formic acid-acetonitrile for gradient elution, with seven markers separated within 55 min. Twenty components were characterized by LC-MS. The validated method exhibited satisfactory linearity, precision, repeatability, stability and recovery. This indicates LLMs can reduce the workload of chromatographic condition exploration and boost the development efficiency of TCM formula analytical methods, supporting intelligent TCM quality control.

items.title: Digital enablement and employee performance in society 5.0: a dual-path model of motivation and exhaustion
items.abstract: Introduction Society 5.0 integrates advanced digital technologies with human-centered work systems, yet its implications for sustainable employee performance remain underexplored. Drawing on Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory, this study examines the relationship between Society 5.0 enablement intensity (S5EI) and sustainable human performance through autonomous motivation and emotional exhaustion, considering human-centric governance capability as a moderator. Methods The study employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyse data collected from 519 employees working in digitally intensive sectors in India. Results The findings indicate that S5EI is positively associated with sustainable human performance, primarily through autonomous motivation. Emotional exhaustion partially offsets this positive effect through competitive mediation. Human-centric governance capability strengthens the relationship between autonomous motivation and sustainable human performance but does not significantly buffer the negative effect of emotional exhaustion. Discussion The findings conceptualize digital enablement as a dual-valence work condition that simultaneously strengthens autonomy-based motivation and increases digital demands, integrating Job Demands–Resources Theory and Self-Determination Theory. The study highlights the importance of participatory digital governance, workload management, and employee recovery measures for supporting sustainable human performance.

items.title: Digital Literacy Of Nursing Students In Clinical Teaching: A Scoping Review Protocol
items.abstract: In an education increasingly mediated by smart technologies, it is essential that nursing students maintain critical thinking and autonomous clinical judgment. Digital literacy goes beyond technical expertise, incorporating an ethical, conscious, and contextualized analysis of the social, political, and epistemological impacts of artificial intelligence. This competence prevents the uncritical use of digital tools and fosters an understanding of their mechanisms, risks, and limitations, including biases and misinformation. In the context of nursing, this approach ensures that technology complements human judgment without compromising safety and person-centered care. Thus, training should be guided by ethical principles, critical reflection, and professional responsibility, preparing future nurses for an increasingly complex and digital clinical landscape. The study participants are nursing students in a clinical teaching setting. The review will follow the JBI methodology and reporting according to PRISMA-ScR. The databases to be searched include CINAHL Plus Complete, MEDLINE Complete Plus, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by unpublished literature in the ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Citation Index (via Web of Science) and RCAAP. Studies in Portuguese, English, and Spanish will be included. Two independent reviewers will perform the analysis, extraction, and synthesis of data using the Rayyan platform. The results will be presented narratively, with tables or figures.

items.title: Digital Transformation Through a Socio‐Technical Systems Lens: Women Leaders' Approaches to Technological Change and Organizational Dynamics
items.abstract: Organizations navigating digital transformation face persistent challenges integrating social and technical elements to support innovation and worker wellbeing. Despite increasing workforce participation, women remain underrepresented in senior leadership roles that shape how this integration occurs, leaving perspectives shaped by gendered organizational experience underexplored within digital transformation research. Drawing on thematic analysis of interviews with sixteen senior women leaders across Australian organizations, this study applies socio‐technical systems theory and a gender‐informed leadership perspective to examine how these leaders understood and navigated the relationship between technical and social domains during digital transformation. Participants treated technical and social considerations as mutually constitutive, enacting their integration through communication, employee participation, human‐centered work design, capability development and ongoing adaptation. Psychosocial safety emerged across technical, social and integration‐focused accounts as a system‐level condition implicated in this process. Together, these findings provide an empirical account of human‐centric transformation within Industry 5.0 and extend socio‐technical systems theory by conceptualizing integration as an enacted process through which technical and social considerations continually shape one another. A gender‐informed analysis further demonstrates the value of gendered organizational experience for understanding how socio‐technical integration is accomplished in practice.

items.title: Disaggregated LLM Inference in Space: A Communication Feasibility Study
items.abstract: Orbital data centers could enable large-scale AI inference, but efficiently serving a frontier language model to many users may require several compute satellites to cooperate over optical links. While disaggregated inference, which splits large language model (LLM) serving across machines, is well established in terrestrial data centers, its viability under the unique constraints of orbital deployments remains an open question. This article investigates how link capacity and satellite separation affect two types of disaggregated LLM serving, in both compact satellite formations and distributed constellations. Prefill-decode disaggregation (PDD) migrates a large KV cache once per request, while attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) exchanges small activations at every mixture-of-experts layer for every generated token. The two respond to distance in different ways. PDD is limited mainly by link capacity and, with fast enough links, tolerates separations of up to a thousand kilometers. AFD is limited mainly by propagation delay, which accumulates layer by layer and forces attention and expert instances within about a kilometer of each other. Based on these results, we propose a hierarchical orbital inference architecture and provide network design guidelines for future orbital data centers, including the role of ground access latency.

items.title: Distúrbios Musculoesqueléticos em Colaboradores de Contact Center: Prevalência e Estratégias de Prevenção Fisioterapêutica na Empresa Ucall (Angola, 2025)
items.abstract: Introdução: O sector de contact center constitui um dos pilares da economia digital, mas impõe aos seus colaboradores riscos ergonómicos e psicossociais elevados, decorrentes da imobilidade prolongada, da repetitividade gestual e da pressão por indicadores de desempenho. Na empresa Ucall, em Angola, a incidência de Distúrbios Musculoesqueléticos Relacionados ao Trabalho (DORT) constitui um desafio relevante à saúde ocupacional. Objetivo: Analisar a prevalência dos distúrbios musculoesqueléticos e discutir estratégias de prevenção fisioterapêutica em colaboradores de contact center na empresa Ucall, no primeiro semestre de 2025. Metodologia: Estudo descritivo, de abordagem mista (quantitativa e qualitativa) e corte transversal, realizado na empresa Ucall (Talatona, Luanda). A amostra, não probabilística e por conveniência, foi composta por 22 colaboradores de uma população de 80. Os dados foram recolhidos remotamente via Google Forms, com recurso ao Questionário Nórdico de Sintomas Osteomusculares (QNSO) e à Escala Visual Analógica (EVA). Resultados: Identificou-se um paradoxo estrutural: embora 72,7% dos postos de trabalho disponham de cadeiras com ajuste técnico, apenas uma minoria dos colaboradores adota posturas adequadas. A coluna lombar (31,8%) e a região dorsal (18,2%) concentraram a maior prevalência de queixas, com níveis médios de dor entre 6 e 8 na escala EVA em quase metade da amostra. A pressão por metas influenciou a tensão muscular em 77,3% dos inquiridos, e 59,1% classificaram as pausas laborais como apenas ligeiramente satisfatórias. Conclusões: A prevalência elevada de DORT na empresa Ucall exige uma estratégia multidimensional de prevenção fisioterapêutica, que integre ergonomia física, gestão da carga mental e educação postural desde a admissão, consolidando a fisioterapia ocupacional como elemento estratégico para a sustentabilidade da saúde no trabalho. Palavras-chave: Distúrbios Musculoesqueléticos; Prevalência; Contact Center; Fisioterapia Ocupacional; Ucall; Angola. ABSTRACT Introduction: The contact center sector is a pillar of the digital economy, but it exposes employees to elevated ergonomic and psychosocial risks arising from prolonged immobility, repetitiveness, and pressure related to performance indicators. At the Ucall company, in Angola, the incidence of Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders (WRMSD) constitutes a relevant occupational health challenge. Objective: To analyze the prevalence of musculoskeletal disorders and to discuss physiotherapeutic prevention strategies among contact center employees at the Ucall company, in the first semester of 2025. Methods: A descriptive study with a mixed quantitative-qualitative approach and a cross-sectional design was conducted at the Ucall company (Talatona, Luanda). The non-probabilistic, convenience sample consisted of 22 employees drawn from a population of 80. Data were collected remotely via Google Forms, using the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ) and the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS). Results: A structural paradox was identified: although 72.7% of workstations were equipped with technically adjustable chairs, only a minority of employees adopted adequate posture. The lumbar spine (31.8%) and thoracic region (18.2%) concentrated the highest prevalence of complaints, with mean pain levels between 6 and 8 on the VAS scale in nearly half of the sample. Pressure for targets influenced muscular tension in 77.3% of respondents, and 59.1% rated work breaks as only slightly satisfactory. Conclusions: The high prevalence of WRMSD at Ucall requires a multidimensional physiotherapeutic prevention strategy integrating physical ergonomics, mental workload management, and postural education from onboarding, consolidating occupational physiotherapy as a strategic element for workplace health sustainability. Keywords: Musculoskeletal Disorders; Prevalence; Contact Center; Occupational Physiotherapy; Ucall; Angola.

items.title: Do Embedding-Map Distances Guide LLM Ideation? Four Tests Against What Came Next
items.abstract: A popular ideation recipe treats an embedding map of existing work as a guide: pick points far from everything and decode them into ideas. I test four ways such distances could guide ideation against what appeared later. (1) Far random directions are not text: no later item reaches a raw cosine above about 0.10 with one (after centring or whitening, 22 of 24 cells stay out of reach), and an LLM decoder shown a target's neighbours, with score-only feedback, writes those neighbours in all six target sets. A neighbour-free search writes coherent text at median cosine 0.57 and 0.47 to interior gaps, beating the nearest existing item on 15 and 14 of 20, but only 0.07 and 0.06 to far points. (2) On k-means cells of a past-only map, the registered hole score mostly tracks cell size and position; three density-based gap scores forecast which cells grow fastest at or below chance (AUC 0.30 to 0.66) and add nothing to momentum in Steam and arXiv, with patents inconclusive; more isolated new Steam games are slightly better reviewed. (3) LLM continuations of arXiv papers stay closer to the source than papers that cite it, under three user prompts and against proposal rewrites (gpt-4o) and April-December 2023 papers (OLMo). Critique lengthens this step beyond content-free revision, replicated on 150 new papers. Revealing a real follow-up's title turns the ideas by 0.032 along a follow-up-specific direction beyond revision; reviewer, oracle and distance feedback add 0.13, 0.08 and 0.34 of that turn (upper bounds 0.46, 0.46, 0.70), and their turn is not separable from revision or their longer step. (4) For inspiration material graded by distance, no inverted U was detected, on an anticipation margin that tracks format more than content. Original tests were registered before running, follow-ups (thirteen requested in two AI-agent reviews) after the main results; all are dated only by local git commits.
