items.title: Does Generative AI Reduce Mental Effort at The Expense of Deep Thinking? An Experimental Investigation of Cognitive Load and Knowledge Retention
items.abstract: The rapid integration of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) into higher education has transformed learning practices, raising critical concerns regarding its influence on cognitive engagement, analytical reasoning, and knowledge retention. This study experimentally examines whether GenAI-assisted learning reduces cognitive load at the expense of deep thinking and sustained knowledge acquisition. A randomized controlled experimental design was employed involving 120 undergraduate students, randomly assigned to an experimental group utilizing ChatGPT (n = 60) and a control group completing equivalent learning activities without AI assistance (n = 60). Participants undertook analytical reading, conceptual problem-solving, and critical reasoning tasks under standardized experimental conditions. Cognitive load was measured using a mental effort rating scale, deep thinking was assessed through rubric-based analytical reasoning evaluations, and knowledge retention was examined using immediate and delayed post-tests administered two weeks apart. Results revealed significantly lower perceived cognitive load among AI-assisted learners (M = 3.42, SD = 1.11) compared with the control group (M = 5.76, SD = 1.24), t(118) = 10.88, p < .001. Conversely, students learning without AI demonstrated superior deep-thinking performance (M = 78.40, SD = 9.65) relative to AI-assisted participants (M = 70.25, SD = 10.82), p < .001. Immediate knowledge retention scores showed comparatively modest differences between the experimental and control groups (82.30% versus 80.10%, respectively). However, delayed retention assessments revealed a substantial performance advantage for the control group (74.60%) over AI-assisted learners (65.20%), indicating greater knowledge deterioration following AI-supported learning. These findings suggest that although GenAI effectively reduces perceived mental effort during academic tasks, such efficiency gains may coincide with diminished analytical engagement and weaker long-term knowledge retention. The study extends cognitive load theory and cognitive offloading perspectives by identifying a potential trade-off between immediate learning efficiency and sustained cognitive development. The findings underscore the importance of pedagogically structured GenAI integration that encourages independent reasoning, active knowledge construction, and meaningful cognitive engagement rather than passive dependence on AI-generated responses. Implications for instructional design, assessment practices, and responsible AI adoption in higher education are discussed.

items.title: Dynamic Thematic Map Generation from Multi-Source Post-Earthquake Data Based on Large Language Models
items.abstract: Within the golden 72 h after an earthquake, the rapid generation of emergency thematic maps is critical for disaster assessment and rescue decision-making, yet it faces core challenges such as the difficulty of reusing experience from historical earthquakes and the weak association among multi-source heterogeneous data. The spatial hallucination inherent in conventional spatial RAG systems can further mislead situational awareness of the affected region and increase decision risk. To address these issues, this paper proposes an adaptive dynamic thematic map generation method that fuses LLMs with Graph RAG for earthquake emergency scenarios. At the knowledge reconstruction level, a dual-channel association constraint mechanism over spatial and semantic channels is designed to link base geographic data, emergency resources, and historical cases across modalities, thereby constructing a directed heterogeneous event-region-resource spatial knowledge graph and achieving spatially grounded semantic consolidation of heterogeneous spatiotemporal multi-source data in emergency scenarios. At the retrieval and reasoning level, asymmetric query rewriting and multi-dimensional parallel recall over graph topology are introduced together with causal constraints of earthquake-triggered spatiotemporal propagation and proactive circuit breaking, which upgrades the text matching of conventional RAG to multi-hop spatiotemporal causal reasoning over the entire cross-domain chain of earthquake emergency response, suppresses spatial hallucination at the source of spatial decision making, and ensures the rigor of historical case reuse. At the collaborative mapping level, a multi-dimensional text fusion model of evolutionary evidence chains is constructed, which converts the discrete reasoning results of the LLM into standardized structured semantics and realizes mechanism-driven mapping of disaster semantics such as seismic intensity and lifeline engineering damage onto emergency thematic map layers. In addition, in-memory and distributed multi-level caching strategies are introduced to reduce the computational response latency when massive data floods in after strong earthquakes. Experiments on real earthquakes such as the Lushan and Luding events show that the proposed method raises the layer match rate to 0.791 (versus 0.295 for the strongest baseline), achieves the best layer-set F1 (0.252), reduces the in-window viewport-center displacement to 21.2 km, and attains a blind-judged semantic accuracy of 0.429 over the full 200-query set (0.881 on in-window queries) against 0.00 for all baselines, while a spatially filtered hybrid baseline reaches only 0.068. Driven by a lightweight 7B model, the cold-start generation of a single thematic map takes only 0.83 min, and the dynamic viewport refresh is kept within 12 s when the cache is activated, which meets the time window requirement for rapid post-earthquake map production. Given the moderate overall semantic accuracy and the disclosed out-of-graph coverage boundary, the method is positioned as an efficient and verifiable decision-support solution whose outputs still require human verification, rather than as a fully autonomous cartographic product.

items.title: Edit Recommendation: Can LLMs Anticipate Edit Requests from Users, and When?
items.abstract: After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. This paper studies whether an LLM can anticipate these requests before they are sent. Such anticipation is useful in practice because it reduces the effort of user review and feedback. We formalize this task as edit recommendation and build EditRecBench, a benchmark for evaluating the performance of LLMs on this task, from real-world conversation logs in WildChat-4.8M. Through benchmarking and failure analysis, we identify a practical challenge that some cases are inherently difficult to predict in real-world settings. To address this, we introduce decision model-based gating to filter out cases where predictions are unlikely to be correct before they are presented to the user. Our trained model outperforms existing decision models and raises pass@5 among shown suggestions by 12--25 points at a gating threshold. Our code is available at https://github.com/ntt-dkiku/llm-edit-recommendation.

items.title: Effect of Facilitated Problem-Based Learning on Intrinsic and Extrinsic Motivation Among Nursing Students in North-East Nigeria
items.abstract: This study investigated the effect of facilitated Problem-Based Learning (PBL) on intrinsic and extrinsic motivation among nursing students in North-East Nigeria. A quasi-experimental pre-test, post-test control group design was adopted. The population comprised 1,065 ND II nursing students from six Colleges of Nursing Science in North-East Nigeria, from which 200 students were selected using a multi-stage sampling procedure. The sample consisted of 100 students in the experimental group exposed to facilitated PBL and 100 students in the control group taught using conventional lecture-based instruction. Data were collected using a 28-item Academic Motivation Questionnaire (AMQ). The instrument demonstrated satisfactory reliability with a Cronbach’s alpha coefficient of 0.84. The experimental group participated in a six-week facilitated PBL intervention involving nursing-related case scenarios, guided questioning, collaborative learning, feedback, and self-directed learning activities. Data were analyzed using means, standard deviations, and t-tests at the 0.05 level of significance. Finding showed that the experimental group recorded an increase in mean intrinsic-motivation scores from 26.30 at pre-test to 50.30 at post-test, compared with an increase from 25.90 to 30.20 in the control group. A significant effect was also found on extrinsic motivation, with the experimental group recording a greater reduction in extrinsic motivation than the control group, t(198) = 8.72, p < .05. therefore, motivation also differed significantly between the facilitated PBL and lecture groups, t(198) = 14.02, p < .001. Furthermore, a significant difference was observed between intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, t(198) = 6.85, p < .001. The study concluded that facilitated PBL is an effective instructional approach for strengthening intrinsic motivation and promoting more self-directed learning among nursing students. It was recommended that nursing institutions should integrate facilitated PBL into their programmes, train educators in effective PBL facilitation, provide adequate learning resources, and emphasize learning activities that foster students’ intrinsic motivation.

items.title: EFFECTS OF VIRTUAL REALITY AND GAMIFICATION ON MOTOR FUNCTION AND TREATMENT ADHERENCE IN POST-STROKE PATIENTS: A LITERATURE REVIEW
items.abstract: Considering that stroke is one of the main causes of physical disability worldwide, with more than 60% of survivors presenting residual motor impairment, and that conventional physical therapy imposes limitations on repetitiveness and adherence, the objective is to analyze the efficacy of virtual reality (VR) and gamification in the physical therapy rehabilitation of post-stroke patients, emphasizing motor function and treatment adherence. Therefore, a narrative/integrative literature review of a descriptive-analytical nature is carried out, with qualitative synthesis of evidence, performed in the BVS/LILACS, SciELO, PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar databases, with an adapted PICO strategy, DeCS/MeSH descriptors and free terms, between 2015 and 2025, in Portuguese and English, which resulted in the inclusion of 18 studies organized into two thematic axes. Thus, it is observed that VR, especially when associated with conventional physical therapy, promotes consistent benefits on upper limb motor function, balance, gait and coordination, with small to moderate effect sizes (SMD 0.32; 95% CI 0.08–0.56) and moderate to low certainty of evidence, and that gamification favors adherence and engagement by increasing intrinsic motivation, although the evidence for this outcome is scarcer and heterogeneous. This allows concluding that VR and gamification are promising and complementary resources to conventional physical therapy, with documented benefits on motor function and relevant potential for treatment adherence, and that Brazilian randomized clinical trials with standardized protocols and validated adherence measurement instruments are recommended.

items.abstract: We audit instruction-hierarchy enforcement across 363 text-in/text-out models from the OpenRouter catalog. The research question we answer with this experiment is which models disclose a protected secret embedded in the system prompt, and through which techniques. Each model guards a secret 16-character flag set in its system prompt, while an artificial intelligence (AI) agent (OpenCode, powered by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash), steered by a human researcher, tries to persuade it to emit the flag. The flag was exfiltrated from 296 of the 363 models, plus four models released after the initial catalog freeze, for 300 captures in total. Of these, 170 involved a non-English language pivot, most often French. Each capture shows that a model ranked a user request above its system instruction at least once. It does not show that the model provably resists untested attacks, nor that it would consistently leak semantically sensitive data, nor that it is vulnerable to harmful-content jailbreaks. For practitioners, we draw three lessons: do not store secrets in system prompts, enforce critical behavior outside the model with output validation and deterministic checks, and do not let a large language model (LLM) judge be the sole decider of consequential outcomes.

items.title: Emerging Research Fronts in Public Relations Scholarship: An Analytical Synthesis of Technological Disruption, Epistemic Diversification, and Disciplinary Self-Examination
items.abstract: This paper presents an analytical synthesis of contemporary research fronts in public relations (PR) scholarship, drawing on recent work in leading journals (Public Relations Review, Journal of Public Relations Research, Corporate Communications: An International Journal), agenda-setting signals from disciplinary bodies (ICA, IPR, PRSA), and 2025–2026 special-issue programs. Seven interrelated research fronts are identified: (a) artificial intelligence adoption, ethics, and disciplinary disruption; (b) disinformation, trust, and organizational resilience; (c) theoretical and methodological pluralism, including de-Westernization; (d) employee communication, advocacy, and internal activism; (e) crisis spillover and contagion; (f) measurement, evaluation, and predictive analytics; and (g) bibliometric self-mapping. The analysis argues that these fronts are shaped by three macro-level forces—technological disruption, epistemic diversification, and disciplinary self-examination—and that the intersections among them constitute the field’s most promising publication spaces. Drawing on recent empirical evidence, including a 277-agency survey of AI adoption across the Arab world (Koa et al., 2025), a longitudinal analysis of 630 fact-checks of disinformation targeting organizations in Spain (Rodríguez Fernández et al., 2026), and a dedicated special issue on crisis spillover (Laufer & Wang, 2024), the synthesis shows that the field’s most successful emerging work does not abandon established PR theory but redeploys it in new empirical territories. The paper concludes with a maturity–opportunity assessment and a strategic map of research gaps to guide manuscript positioning in Q1/Q2 outlets during the 2026–2027 publication cycle.

items.title: Emotionally Aware AI Chatbots for Adolescents: A Review of Psychological Principles for Learning, Calibrated Trust, and Healthy Human–AI Interaction
items.abstract: Conversational artificial intelligence now belongs to ordinary adolescent life, but the psychological research that should guide its design spreads over fields which seldom cite each other. Research on adolescent development, on misinformation susceptibility, on trust in automation, on chatbot-supported learning and on companion-chatbot overreliance has grown up separately, and each of these areas answers only part of the question of how a general-purpose chatbot should talk to a teenager. This paper brings together twenty-one sources from developmental psychology, human factors, human-computer interaction and educational technology, in order to show what is now known about adolescent chatbot interaction and what this means for conversational design. Three results appear repeatedly in this research. First, adolescence is a design context of its own, not a smaller version of adulthood, since reward sensitivity, social influence and emotional regulation are still developing, while exposure to persuasive conversational systems has already reached almost everyone. Second, trust in a chatbot changes behavior in ways that can be measured; thus, the proper design target is calibrated trust rather than maximal trust. Third, the failure modes that matter most for adolescent users, that is, hallucination, sycophancy and unwarranted confidence, originate in the model; the user is not their source. From these results this paper consolidates ten conversational design principles into four clusters, namely epistemic calibration, metacognitive scaffolding, bounded emotional support and autonomy preservation. The framework here is a conceptual synthesis and puts forward testable predictions, but it has not been empirically validated.

items.title: Energy-harvesting wearable patch for real-time athletes’ risk detection
items.abstract: Athletes are often at high risk of sudden and severe injury or illness during training sessions due to a lack of safety measures. Failure to monitor health conditions and vital signs during training can result in serious consequences for athletes. Currently, several devices in the market measure vital signs and provide them as raw data; however, they do not prioritize the athlete’s safety and often offer limited feedback on their health condition. Additionally, many of these devices lack ergonomic designs, which limit the athlete’s mobility. This wearable health monitoring device was designed to be both lightweight and cost-effective. It collects and tracks health metrics while providing real-time feedback to the user via an application to support the athlete’s safety. A key feature is the utilization of energy harvesting technology to power the system, which includes a heart rate sensor, core body temperature sensor, and sweat sensor. Furthermore, the acquired data are analyzed using a developed algorithm to detect abnormal and critical health conditions such as dehydration, overtraining syndrome, exertional heat illnesses, and heart attacks risk indicators. These critical data points, which exceed normal ranges, are classified into two alarm levels: Warning Level and Critical Level. Ultimately, the data are transmitted via Wi-Fi to a mobile application, which provides information about the athlete’s health status and guidance to ensure their safety.

items.title: Engagement Mediates Virtual Reality Pain Relief: A Within-Subject Analysis
items.abstract: Interactive virtual reality (VR) reduces acute pain, but the reasons it works are usually assumed rather than directly tested. VR experiences differ widely in how physically and cognitively demanding they are. It is therefore unclear whether relief comes mainly from physical activity or from cognitive engagement. In this study, 29 healthy adults were exposed to a controlled painful stimulus while experiencing one non-interactive baseline and three interactive VR tasks that varied in physical effort. After each trial, participants rated their pain relief, immersion, attention, and how active they felt. The three tasks did not differ in pain relief, despite differing in physical demand, which does not support physical exertion as the main factor. Participants’ ratings of immersion, attention, and activity combined into a single measure of engagement, and a Bayesian within-subject mediation analysis estimated that this engagement accounted for most of the pain relief. This held even when physical activity was excluded from the engagement measure, which points to cognitive engagement rather than physical effort. Individuals who engaged more deeply also tended to report greater pain relief. In this VR setup, pain relief was therefore associated mainly with cognitive engagement rather than physical activity. Because engagement was measured rather than manipulated, this pathway remains correlational. The results nonetheless suggest that VR pain applications should be designed for engagement rather than physical demand.

items.title: Ergonomic issues in vertical farming systems: a PRISMA-informed narrative review
items.abstract: Vertical farming (VF) represents a transformative approach to agricultural production utilizing multi-tiered, controlled-environment systems, yet it introduces unique ergonomic challenges distinct from conventional agriculture. This literature review synthesizes current evidence on ergonomic issues in vertical farming systems, alongside evidence from indoor farming and broader controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) systems, examining musculoskeletal disorder (MSD) prevalence, risk factors, assessment methodologies, and intervention strategies. Agricultural workers in greenhouse and indoor farming environments experience MSD prevalence rates of 50.9% to 89.3%, with the lower back, shoulders, knees, and neck most commonly affected. Available evidence suggests that vertical farming may present distinctive ergonomic challenges, including multi-tiered configurations associated with overhead reaching, lower-tier access constraints, repetitive precision tasks, environmental stressors, and complex human-technology interactions. However, much of the current evidence is inferred from greenhouse and broader controlled-environment agriculture systems. While traditional ergonomic assessment tools (RULA, REBA, OWAS) and advanced methods (EMG) have been applied in agricultural contexts, their adaptation to vertical farming remains limited. Current interventions show promise through workspace optimization, tool redesign, automation, and participatory ergonomics approaches. However, significant knowledge gaps persist regarding longitudinal health outcomes, human-automation interaction, cognitive ergonomics, and socioeconomic dimensions specific to vertical farming. This review highlights the emerging need for human-centered design principles in VF system development to ensure worker health, safety, and operational sustainability.

items.title: Ergonomic Setup for Trans‐Radial Procedures Using a Height‐Adjustable Trolley in the Angiography Suite
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Trans-radial access (TRA), while experiencing varying global adoption among interventional radiologists, offers potential benefits including reduced access-site bleeding, accelerated patient ambulation, and decreased overall healthcare expenditures compared with trans-femoral access (TFA). However, TRA introduces distinct occupational ergonomic burdens, including asymmetrical arm abduction, working height discrepancies with standard angiographic tables, and inadequate support for long microcatheters and guidewires. These biomechanical constraints heighten operator fatigue and increase the cumulative risk of work-related musculoskeletal disorders. TECHNIQUE: A mobile, height-adjustable trolley-conceptually adapted from ergonomic sit-stand workstations-was integrated into the angiography suite workflow. Arranged parallel to the patient in a Z-shaped spatial configuration, the trolley is linked to the patient's outstretched access arm using an extended sterile drape to establish a stable, continuous sterile working platform. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: This technical configuration restores neutral operator posture, mitigates lumbar torsion and cervical strain, eliminates sterile field breaches from suspended equipment, and increases the physical working distance from primary scatter radiation sources. Furthermore, the elevated surface facilitates gravity-assisted administration of dense Yttrium-90 microspheres during radioembolization and prevents rotational interference during cone-beam computed tomography acquisitions. CONCLUSION: The implementation of a height-adjustable trolley provides a simple, cost-effective, and highly adaptable ergonomic solution that optimizes procedural efficiency, sterile field integrity, and radiation safety during trans-radial interventional procedures.

items.title: Ergonomics-Integrated Generative AI for Personalized Work Design in Aging and Diversifying Industrial Workforces
items.abstract: In industrialized countries, rapid population aging and declining birth rates have made labor shortages a critical issue in industrial workplaces. Without actively utilizing elderly workers, persons with disabilities, and foreign workers, on-site operations risk becoming unsustainable. Addressing this challenge requires not only technological innovation but also a transdisciplinary engineering approach that integrates human, social, and industrial system perspectives. This study proposes a personalized work design framework that combines generative artificial intelligence (AI) and ergonomics to enable inclusive and sustainable industrial operations. The proposed framework utilizes individual attribute data—such as age-related physical characteristics, functional limitations, work experience, and language proficiency—to generate task configurations tailored to diverse worker groups. Ergonomic principles are systematically embedded into the generative AI model to adapt task sequences, work postures, workload distribution, and operational instructions according to individual capabilities and constraints. From an engineering perspective, the framework integrates data-driven AI modeling, human factors engineering, and production system design to dynamically optimize the interaction between workers and industrial environments. A case study conducted in a manufacturing-related setting demonstrates that the proposed approach reduces physical strain and cognitive workload while maintaining or improving productivity and operational stability. The results indicate that AI-driven ergonomic task personalization is particularly effective in enabling the participation of elderly workers, persons with disabilities, and foreign workers in on-site industrial work. This research highlights the value of transdisciplinary engineering in addressing complex societal challenges posed by demographic change. By bridging generative AI, ergonomics, and industrial engineering, the proposed framework provides a scalable and human-centered solution for designing adaptive workplaces and supporting long-term workforce sustainability in aging and diversifying societies.

items.title: Evaluating Authorization and Trust Boundaries in Agentic Orchestration Frameworks
items.abstract: Agentic AI systems extend large language models with tools, memory, and multi-agent collaboration, introducing security risks at orchestration boundaries. These risks depend on how identities are represented, operations are authorized, and instructions or information propagate between components. We evaluate LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, and OpenClaw through twelve experiments mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications using a common LLM (gpt-4o-mini). The experiments cover prompt injection, unauthorized resource access and command execution, memory poisoning, and inter-agent trust and identity attacks. Adversarial inputs induced unauthorized tool invocation, while tool chaining, stale filesystem validation, encoded instructions, and inter-agent delegation exposed weaknesses in authorization across component boundaries. Memory poisoning showed that untrusted state can influence responses, a risk distinct from conventional access-control violations. In the evaluated protected configurations, explicit authorization, controlled capability assignment, filesystem containment, and execution safeguards prevented specific unauthorized operations. The findings emphasize preserving authorization and information-trust boundaries throughout agentic workflows rather than treating framework capabilities or model-level instructions as sufficient security guarantees.

items.title: Evaluating Cultural Reasoning and Robustness in LLMs for Spanish Political Discourse
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to interpret, generate, and mediate public-facing language, which makes their reliability especially consequential in politically sensitive settings. Although sentiment analysis is a common task in this area, affective meaning in social media discourse is often conveyed through culturally situated and pragmatically indirect cues that are not well captured by label-centric evaluation alone. In this paper, we evaluate the robustness of LLMs for sentiment analysis of Spanish political discourse from social media, with emphasis on culturally situated affective interpretation. We introduce a diagnostic protocol that combines three independent human annotation views into Gold and Ambiguous subsets, and extends the corpus with a Synthetic subset built from sentiment-flipped counterfactuals selected through model-conditioned perplexity and LLM-as-a-judge criteria. Using this framework, we compare proprietary and open-weight models under zero-shot and few-shot prompting, focusing on predictive robustness across human agreement conditions and counterfactual shift. Our results show that annotation ambiguity and counterfactual perturbation reveal failure modes that conventional evaluation on the original corpus tends to obscure. GPT-4.1-mini remains the most stable among the evaluated models, whereas the two smaller open-weight models degrade more markedly under synthetic perturbations, and few-shot prompting provides only limited gains. Overall, the paper contributes a reproducible protocol for robustness-oriented evaluation in political sentiment analysis, an empirical characterization of model behavior under ambiguity and sentiment-flipped counterfactuals, and a publicly available Spanish social media dataset with three-way human sentiment annotations.

items.title: Evaluating large language models for quality control in research ethics review
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) could streamline research ethics and governance review by automating routine quality control checks. This study assessed Claude 3.5 Sonnet, ChatGPT4o, and Microsoft CoPilot in evaluating participant information sheets against Health Research Authority standards. Six clinical trial applications were processed using 32 standardised queries, with accuracy, processing time, error rates, and response quality assessed by two blinded reviewers. Claude showed the highest accuracy, detected more deviations from guidance, and had the fastest processing time (7.17 ± 0.68 min vs. ChatGPT 13.58 ± 2.2 min, CoPilot 23.25 ± 6.21 min). Hallucination rates were lowest in Claude, followed by ChatGPT and CoPilot. Claude also received the highest response quality ratings (77.6% “very good” vs. ChatGPT 56.7%, CoPilot 45.2%). While all three models were capable, Claude consistently outperformed the others, demonstrating the potential of LLM-assisted quality control while emphasizing the need for human oversight.

items.title: Evidence Diet: When Graph Evidence Helps LLMs Rank Competing Candidates
items.abstract: When several candidates have graph support, does it matter which candidate receives which supporter and path counts? We study how LLM rankers use collaborative evidence on Amazon Books and MovieTV. Swapping user-level evidence degrades ranking, while matched item substitutions have little effect. On fixed clean-trained checkpoints, unrelated catalog text lowers Hit@1 from 44.77% to 38.70%, with 99.9% of rankings still valid. Across all three paired seeds, the NDCG@5 difference between count and path prompts was larger after count training than after path training. Degree matching preserves target paths while giving more rivals support. Across the full degree-matched development pools, adding candidate-level graph records to history improves NDCG@5 by 2.28 points on Books and 2.54 on MovieTV. When the target and a rival both have support, path- and count-trained rankers benefit from retaining counts. On these development queries, adding counts numerically to history scores outperforms presenting them as text. For count-trained rankers, exchanging intact count pairs among supported candidates preserves support and token length, yet lowers NDCG@5 by 4.06 points on 141 Books queries and 3.26 on 104 MovieTV queries. A frozen evaluation on 274 previously unused Books users with supported targets and rivals confirms the attribution effect: correct assignment improves pairwise accuracy by 6.07 percentage points (95% CI [4.18, 8.00]).

items.title: Experiences of female police officers from the psychodynamic of work perspective
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to analyze pleasure, suffering and defensive strategies among civil police officers at specialized police stations for women, based on the psychodynamics of work. Design/methodology/approach This is a qualitative study with 30 civil police officers in Ceará, Brazil. Data were collected through interviews and analyzed using sense nuclei analysis. Findings Pleasure relates to identity, recognition, practical intelligence and collaboration; suffering relates to workload, violence, institutional constraints and gender discrimination. Subjective conditions predominate. Individual defenses address suffering; collective strategies mobilize and strengthen officers but have limited capacity to prevent illness. Sisterhood emerges as resistance and collective empowerment. Practical implications Mental health monitoring, dialogue and gender equity are recommended. Social implications Findings reinforce public policies on mental health and equity. Originality/value This study extends the psychodynamics of work by highlighting the ambivalence of compensation and repression and proposing sisterhood as collective action beyond adaptation, fostering resistance and transformation.

items.title: Exploring user experience design for third restrooms: from inclusive perspective
items.abstract: Third restrooms assist the elderly, young children, and people with mobility impairments. As a key service hub in public spaces, their indoor design directly impacts user satisfaction, yet unmet diverse needs hinder the experience. This study developed a four-stage, eight-activity inclusive design framework. Integrating the AEIOU–Kano model, it compared international standards and conducted field research visiting 20 third restrooms across China. Focusing on five typical user groups—families with young children, caregivers of the elderly, wheelchair users, people with visual impairments, and people with temporary disabilities—the study identified needs and established an evaluation indicator system. It then proposed optimization solutions for spatial layout and facility configuration, validated using Jack simulation. Results indicate the integrated model effectively supports need identification and design decisions, and simulations verified ergonomic adequacy across different body types. These findings provide theoretical and practical foundations for the ergonomic optimization and inclusive design of third restrooms in public spaces, offering guidance for an inclusive service system within public spaces.

items.title: External resilience controls as sociotechnical governance: an extension of dynamic capabilities theory under externally driven volatility
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how organizations construct governance responses to externally driven volatility by embedding external signals into control practices. Focusing on climate exposed agricultural firms, this study extends dynamic capabilities theory (DCT) by developing external resilience controls (ERCs) as a sociotechnical governance construct that illuminates how firms make volatility actionable through formal control routines. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a pragmatic constructivist design science orientation, this study combines six years of financial and operational context (2019–2024) with a longitudinal interpretive content analysis of annual report and sustainability disclosures (2022–2024) from five major agricultural firms. An interpretive design approach enables the systematic synthesis of disclosed organizational practices into a conceptual framework. Findings ERCs emerge as sociotechnical governance arrangements that translate external volatility into organizationally meaningful routines and actionable dynamic capabilities. These arrangements materialize through digital sensing infrastructures, traceability systems, scenario thresholds and board-level oversight that collectively shape how firms interpret and respond to climate anomalies, regulatory shifts and technological change. ERCs reveal resilience as an ongoing process of constructing, stabilizing and legitimizing responses to external volatility. Practical implications ERCs offer practitioners an analytic framework to operationalize dynamic capabilities by integrating digital tools and governance structures. They show how firms convert external volatility into actionable sensing, seizing and reconfiguring routines, enabling adaptive decision-making without relying on rigid control mechanisms. Originality/value This study advances qualitative management scholarship by conceptualizing ERCs as sociotechnical governance constructs. It contributes to strategy research by extending DCT, showing how dynamic capabilities are enacted through the interplay of digital infrastructures, institutional pressures, and organizational sensemaking.

items.title: FaceJev: Direct Visual Decisions for Face Forgery Detection
items.abstract: Face forgery detection methods often perform well on seen manipulations but generalize poorly to unseen ones. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can recognize facial parts and assess their visual plausibility. Existing MLLM-based methods typically express these judgments through textual explanations, but seldom treat individual part decisions as explicit learning targets. We present FaceJev, an MLLM-based method for face forgery detection through direct visual decisions. Following the Jev formulation, FaceJev answers eight independent questions about facial parts using a shared image encoding and reads anomaly probabilities from the native answer logits. A face is classified as forged if any part is predicted to be abnormal, directly linking the detection result to the part decisions. We construct PartForensics, a dataset of approximately 160k images with binary anomaly targets for the eight facial parts, to supervise these decisions. We further propose FS-GRPO, which optimizes each part decision through an exact reward comparison with its alternative, using both detection and part rewards. FaceJev outperforms the strongest baseline by 7.25 percentage points on unseen manipulations. Extensive ablation studies validate our design choices and the effectiveness of the main components.

items.title: Farol do conhecimento: localização de expertise e conexão profissionalna gestão do conhecimento da Petrobras
items.abstract: This article analyzes the Knowledge Lighthouse, the name Petrobras gives to the knowledge management practice commonly known as Yellow Pages. The solution is a business intelligence dashboard that integrates corporate data and professional records to locate expertise by knowledge area or by person. A qualitative and descriptive approach was adopted through a single case study and bibliographic and documentary analysis. The theoretical framework combines knowledge management, transactive memory, competence mapping, intellectual capital, communities of practice, and sociotechnical systems. The study describes the dashboard’s conception, its SAP/SIRH data sources, daily D-1 updating, search and profile detail views, query paths, and corporate access. The analytical findings indicate that the solution may improve expert findability, reduce search costs, foster learning and knowledge integration, and support critical knowledge management, team formation, innovation, internal mobility, succession, and organizational memory. Its effectiveness, however, depends on a governed taxonomy, complete and current data, trust, participation, workflow integration, data protection, and value-oriented evaluation. The study concludes that the Knowledge Lighthouse should operate as an infrastructure for discovery and connection, complemented by human validation and linked to communities, repositories, and knowledgetransfer practices, rather than being converted into an automatic employee assessment mechanism.

items.title: FMint-SDE: A Multimodal Foundation Model for Accelerating Numerical Simulation of SDEs via Error Correction
items.abstract: Fast and accurate simulation of dynamical systems is a fundamental challenge across scientific and engineering domains. Traditional numerical integrators often face a trade-off between accuracy and computational efficiency, while existing neural network–based approaches typically require training a separate model for each case. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a novel multimodal foundation model for large-scale simulations of differential equations: FMint-SDE (Foundation Model based on Initialization for stochastic differential equations). Based on a decoder-only transformer with in-context learning, FMint-SDE leverages numerical and textual modalities to learn a universal error-correction scheme. It is trained using prompted sequences of coarse solutions generated by conventional solvers, enabling broad generalization across diverse systems. We evaluate our models on a suite of challenging SDE benchmarks spanning applications in molecular dynamics, mechanical systems, finance, and biology. Experimental results show that our approach achieves a superior accuracy-efficiency tradeoff compared to classical solvers, underscoring the potential of FMint-SDE as a general-purpose simulation tool for dynamical systems. Reproducibility of computational results. This paper has been awarded the “SIAM Reproducibility Badge: Code and Data Available” as a recognition that the authors have followed reproducibility principles valued by SISC and the scientific computing community. Code and data that allow readers to reproduce the results in this paper are available at https://github.com/margotyjx/FMint-SDE and in the supplementary materials ( M181717_Supplementary_Materials_1.pdf [7.87MB], FMint-SDE-main.zip [206KB]), linked from the main article webpage. items.title: Formally verified harness for Shor's order finding algorithm with $O(n^{2+ε})$ gate cost
items.abstract: It is commonly understood that factoring a general $n$-bit biprime via Shor's order finding algorithm requires $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$ gates by leveraging schoolbook integer arithmetics for addition and multiplication. Recent developments in quantum arithmetic circuits leveraging recursive Toom-Cook schemes have improved the cost scaling to $O(n^{2+ε})$. Here $ε>0$ depends on algorithm implementation details of the recursive multiplication steps, which allow for a vast number of design choices. The challenge in navigating such design space also presents an opportunity for demonstrating innovative practices in quantum software engineering in the era of open agentic science. We present a formally verified harness that ingests a design specification (namely a "policy" that describes a recursive circuit design scheme) from an external source, which may be an AI agent, and produces a set of formalized proofs covering mathematical correctness of the algorithm implementation, asymptotic scaling of the end-to-end gate cost, as well as the correctness of translating the verified algorithm to a detailed circuit implementation with an intermediate representation. The harness is published as an open challenge where human researchers and AI agents can search for more efficient factoring circuits while retaining machine-checked guarantees of correctness and end-to-end asymptotic complexity.

items.title: From Apology to Action: Apologies, Compensation, and Cooperation in LLM Agents
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can make decisions that affect other agents, but what happens after a harmful or unsuccessful interaction remains poorly understood. We investigate whether apologies by LLM agents are associated with subsequent cooperative behaviour, using controlled Prisoner's Dilemma experiments with four commercial models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Mistral Large 3). Across payoff conditions, we examine when agents apologise, the reasons they provide, and the actions that follow. We also examine how access to one round of interaction history affects behaviour and, in a second experiment, whether and how agents offer compensation alongside their apologies. Apology behaviour differed substantially across models and preceding interaction outcomes, and verbal expressions of cooperation did not always align with subsequent actions. Notably, Claude Opus 4.8 apologised even after mutual cooperation, while Mistral Large 3 apologised after being exploited but continued to defect even when its opponent cooperated. After unilateral defection, positively compensated apologies from GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro were followed by mutual cooperation, unlike those from Claude and Mistral. Our findings suggest that apologies, compensation, and strategic behaviour are distinct: conciliatory messages may precede continued defection, while costly apologies may go unanswered. This has important implications for the study of machine behaviour and human-AI interactions, as verbal signals alone may not reliably reflect an AI system's subsequent actions.

items.title: From ethical knowing to ethical becoming: rethinking accounting ethics education in the age of artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Purpose Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly performs the cognitive tasks that accounting ethics education has treated as central to ethical competence. This paper aims to reconceptualise ethical competence as ethical becoming, the ongoing formation of the dispositions and judgement required for answerable professional practice. Design/methodology/approach Through theory synthesis, the paper integrates virtue ethics, Vallor’s account of technomoral virtue, professional identity formation theory and socialising conceptions of accountability. Four practice scenarios set in South Africa’s International Financial Reporting Standards–based accounting environment illustrate the framework against a knowledge-transmission account of ethical competence. Findings Ethical becoming is expressed through practical wisdom, moral courage, relational accountability and situated professional judgement. Relational accountability grounds the other capacities, and situated professional judgement brings them together in decisions answerable to those they affect. The capacities develop through participation, rehearsal, reflective practice and mentorship within communities of practice, in an AI-enabled environment that can remove or open opportunities to exercise ethical judgement. Research limitations/implications The framework is conceptual and illustrated in one jurisdiction. Its four propositions require testing with students, trainees and practitioners. Practical implications The framework informs curriculum design, teaching and assessment, illustrated through a worked example, and supports professional bodies and organisations in building ethical formation into competency frameworks and workplace learning. Social implications Forming professionals who remain answerable to investors, communities and others affected by professional judgement strengthens the public trust on which accounting’s public-interest mandate depends. Originality/value Drawing on Vallor’s technomoral virtue ethics, this paper connects ethical formation and AI-enabled accounting, explaining how practical wisdom, moral courage and answerability form when AI performs part of professional work.

items.title: From extension to the reconfiguration of the human: artificial intelligence as an environment in media ecology
items.abstract: Purpose The main objective is to analyze the sociotechnical implications of Artificial Intelligence as it transitions from an assistive model (“copilot”) to an agentic and autonomous model. It seeks to explore how this new environment redefines human identity, authorship, and the autonomy of thought in the face of total technical integration. Method The study employs a theoretical-critical analysis methodology based on Media Ecology as a metadiscipline. It adopts a systemic and longitudinal perspective that traces the evolution of human interfaces from the control of fire to the present. As a primary diagnostic tool, it uses the McLuhan Tetrad to examine what AI enhances, obsolesces, retrieves, and reverses into. Findings AI as an Exocortex: AI functions as an external layer of brain processing that tends to reshape our decisions, tastes, and analyses. Autonomous and Agentic Model: Unlike previous media that functioned as a human reflection, AI contributes to creating an autonomous model capable of generating culture and narratives independently. The “Black Box” Effect: The inscrutable nature of neural networks hinders transparency and oversight in critical areas like justice or healthcare. Displacement of Judgment: There is a progressive “anesthesia” where human critical judgment is displaced toward automated algorithmic processes. Implications Cognitive Amputation: By delegating decision-making and technical labor to machines, humans risk the atrophy of their own critical and creative capacities. Crisis of Truth: AI can “hack” the operating system of civilization (language), creating “reality bubbles” where “truth” becomes a byproduct of the algorithm rather than human dialectics. Dictatorship of Efficiency: The velocity of AI exceeds the response capacity of democratic institutions, potentially rendering “freedom of choice” an obsolete concept in favor of automated efficiency. Value The text provides a critical outlook that moves beyond technical optimism, proposing an “ethics of selective disconnection”. Its value lies in defending human imperfection, ambiguity, and silence as essential non-optimizable elements that must be preserved against the binary logic of AI.

items.title: From Vision to Interaction: Evaluating Dynamic Social Intelligence of VLM Agents in ALIVE-World
items.abstract: As AI agents are increasingly deployed in real-world applications and take on social roles, dynamic social intelligence, the ability to continuously perceive multimodal cues, infer latent cognitive states, intervene through embodied actions, and ultimately achieve social goals, has become essential. However, existing evaluations largely fragment social intelligence into text-based abstractions, static reasoning tasks, or embodied simulators that lack social dynamics. These approaches fail to capture the multimodal, continuous, and interpersonal complexity of authentic human interactions. To bridge this gap, we introduce ALIVE-World, an embodied simulation environment supporting dynamic multimodal interactions encompassing egocentric vision, language, and non-verbal action. To provide socially grounded interactive feedback, we populate this environment with counterpart agents driven by a profile-conditioned, dual-system (intuitive-affective and logical-cognitive) architecture. Building upon this platform, we propose ALIVE-Bench to transform the assessment of social intelligence into a trackable quantitative framework. By deeply leveraging underlying environmental states and agents' internal variables, ALIVE-Bench systematically evaluates Vision-Language Model (VLM) agents across four critical dimensions: perception, understanding, influence, and outcome. Extensive evaluations reveal that dynamic social intelligence is fundamentally multi-dimensional and scenario-dependent. We identify a critical bottleneck between upstream perception and downstream social intervention, exposing VLM vulnerabilities in fine-grained proxemic awareness, adaptive intervention, and multi-party coordination. By uncovering these limitations and the diverse interaction strategies they produce, this benchmark provides actionable insights for the future behavioral alignment of multimodal agents.

items.title: Gamified Resistance and the Reproduction of Platform Control: Jiacan in China's Food‐Delivery Sector
items.abstract: This article examines Jiacan , Chinese food‐delivery riders' term for retaining or consuming undelivered food. Drawing on digital ethnography of rider chat groups, interviews, Douyin vlogs and public discussion threads, it shows how grievance‐linked Jiacan acquires resistant meaning through customer‐mediated disputes, digital circulation and peer evaluation. We develop Gamified Resistance to describe resistance socially organised through shared procedures, risk–reward calculations and judgments about acceptable conduct. The analysis identifies three pathways through which resistance may reproduce platform control: proceduralised rule‐navigation, triadic displacement toward customers and priced dissent. Riders can obtain immediate relief or retaliation while sustaining dependence on platform adjudication, customer‐mediated relations and sanctions. Control reproduction remains provisional: peer judgments, public scrutiny and customer claims can regulate participation and channel disputes, but also challenge the practice or redirect conflict toward the platform.

items.title: Gender and Valuation in Venture Capital
items.abstract: Recent work in the sociology of finance draws attention to the speculative valuations associated with venture capital (VC) investments. Yet the fact that the VC ecosystem is dominated by men is persistently overlooked. This paper redresses the largely gender-blind sociology of valuation in financing by focusing on investors and startups in the much-hyped market of Artificial Intelligence. Our aim is to show how gender matters in performative market-making. Drawing on in-depth interviews with men and women involved in high-tech financing, we analyse the structural impediments to successful female pitching, valuation, and work in VC. By zooming in on the microprocesses of financialization, valuation and assessment, we shed new light on how the mechanisms involved in the assessment of high-tech startups impact female founders. Our study finds that women are excluded through shifting reference to one of several social mechanisms in a practice we call 'rationale roulette': reliance upon future-oriented narratives that can only be persuasively performed by men, embeddedness within homogenous male-dominated networks, and relegation of feminized pathways to the sidelines. In the highly uncertain world of VC investments, valuations based on gender ultimately transmute into a hedge against risk. We conclude with implications for economic sociologies of finance, the innovation sector, and sociotechnical systems, as scholars must recognize the constitutive status of gender and other social characteristics to better understand local valuation mechanisms and their implications for the sector.

items.title: Gender in the Governance of Educational AI: A Critical Discourse Analysis of International Frameworks for AI Use in Teaching and Learning
items.abstract: International policy frameworks governing the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in education shape national policies and classroom practices. This research applies the three-dimensional Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA) model of Fairclough (2010) to three important international documents which are UNESCO Guidance for Generative AI in Education and Research (2023), European Commission Guidelines on the Ethical Use of AI (2025) and UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Gender Report: Technology on Her Terms (2024). This study investigates how gender is framed, which gender identities are centred or marginalized, how risks and opportunities are positioned in governance language, and what ideological assumptions underlie governance language through systematic analyses of lexical choices, transitivity structures, modality patterns, and ideological assumptions. It has been found that there is a significant discursive divergence across the data. Two of the three documents use strategies to make women and girls structurally invisible despite gender equity commitments. The third document employs feminist-structural framing that names certain gender identities and documents gender-specific harms. It also approaches gender inequality as a systemic condition requiring institutional accountability. According to the study, the gap between what is declared or professed and what is discursively enacted with regard to equity principles reflects a failure of governance with ramifications for policy. Suggestions are given for creating gender responsive frameworks for education governance for AI.

items.title: Generative AI and the Crisis of Higher Education Assessments: Examining 'AI-Proofing' Strategies for College-Level Assessments
items.abstract: Higher education is confronting an academic-integrity challenge unlike any in its history. Students can now outsource homework, take-home assignments, and online examinations to large language models (LLMs) that complete them in seconds. Existing research on evaluating LLM performance on academic assessments has focused largely on standardized examinations, or on questions from college-level courses drawn from a single discipline. Far less is known about how LLMs perform on college-level assessment questions spanning multiple disciplines, that instructors have purposely designed to be AI-resistant, and about which features of such questions, if any, meaningfully constrain LLM performance. We address this gap by collecting 75 questions from authentic college coursework assessments, spanning 17 disciplines, which were contributed by 37 faculty members from ten U.S. universities and one U.K. university. Of these, 61 questions were intentionally designed by faculty members to be 'LLM-proof', while the remaining 14 questions were sourced from online courses. We then (i) evaluate three state-of-the-art LLMs' ability to correctly answer these questions with and without supplementary course materials; (ii) identify five strategies, through thematic analysis, that faculty used to make their questions harder for LLMs to solve; and (iii) test whether these strategies impact LLMs' ability to answer the questions accurately. Our experimental results show that the best-performing model scored approximately 83% without supplementary course materials and 85% with them, and we observed noteworthy differences across models, answer formats, and instructor tweaking strategies. We discuss implications for assessment design, academic-integrity policy, and the broader ethics of deploying LLMs in educational settings.

items.title: Gobernanza, captura regulatoria y economía política de la transición nucleoeléctrica en el Perú: Análisis institucional tras la Ley N.° 32560
items.abstract: Resumen La promulgación de la Ley N.° 32560 en marzo de 2026 y el subsecuente proceso de reorganización institucional del sector nuclear peruano han abierto una nueva frontera en la política energética nacional: la generación nucleoeléctrica mediante Reactores Modulares Pequeños (SMR) y el aprovechamiento de recursos uraníferos. El presente artículo analiza, desde la economía política y la sociología de las organizaciones, la tensión estructural entre la promoción del negocio energético y la necesidad de crear una autoridad supervisora nuclear autónoma. A partir de la teoría de la captura regulatoria y la gobernanza de tecnologías de alto riesgo, se examina el conflicto de intereses inherente al diseño institucional tradicional, donde un mismo organismo concentra funciones de fomento tecnológico y fiscalización radiológica. Se concluye que la viabilidad económica y la legitimidad social de la industria nuclear en el Perú dependen de establecer una separación institucional estricta, blindada contra la captura corporativa y sustentada en una supervisión sociotécnica independiente. Palabras clave: Regulación nuclear, captura regulatoria, economía política de la energía, Ley N.° 32560, reactores modulares pequeños (SMR), gobernanza energética, Perú. Abstract The enactment of Law No. 32560 in March 2026 and the subsequent institutional reorganization of the Peruvian nuclear sector have opened a new frontier in national energy policy: nuclear power generation through Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) and the exploitation of uranium resources. This paper analyzes, from the perspectives of political economy and organizational sociology, the structural tension between energy business promotion and the need to establish an autonomous nuclear supervisory authority. Grounded in regulatory capture theory and the governance of high-risk technologies, it examines the conflict of interest inherent in traditional institutional designs, where a single agency concentrates technological promotion and radiological oversight functions. It concludes that the economic viability and social legitimacy of the nuclear industry in Peru depend on establishing a strict institutional separation, shielded against corporate capture and grounded in independent sociotechnical oversight. items.title: GPRM: Global Perspective Process Reward Model
items.abstract: Process Reward Models (PRMs) are widely used for step-level evaluation of multi-step reasoning in large language models, but existing methods are often limited by weak historical dependency modeling and insufficient global awareness. They typically fail to leverage prior step evaluations for coherent judgment and lack visibility into subsequent reasoning, leading to suboptimal assessment of intermediate steps. To address this issue, we propose the Global Perspective Process Reward Model (GPRM), which jointly models the problem, previous reasoning steps and their evaluations, the current step, and future steps to enable history-aware and globally informed process evaluation. We further introduce a structured evaluation framework along four dimensions---look back, look ahead, self-check, and goal alignment---to assess prior consistency, future plausibility, step validity, and task alignment. Based on this framework, we construct datasets for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (GRPO). Experiments show that, despite using less training data and smaller model sizes, GPRM outperforms strong baseline models by 7.8 and 5.4 points on PRMBench and ProcessBench, respectively. GPRM also generalizes well across tasks, surpassing the GPT-4.1 baseline on Agent Error Bench, improving strong baselines by around 4 points under test-time scaling (TTS), and achieving competitive performance on PPE.

items.title: GranularGPT: Natural-Language-Driven End-to-End Discrete Element Method Simulations
items.abstract: Discrete element method (DEM) simulations are widely used to investigate granular and particulate systems, but their application often requires specialized expertise in particle physics, numerical modelling, and simulation post-processing. Large language models (LLMs) offer new opportunities to simplify these workflows by enabling users to interact with simulation tools through natural language. This study offers GranularGPT, an LLM-assisted agentic framework for end-to-end DEM simulation workflows, from natural-language problem descriptions to simulation execution and automated post-processing. The framework enables users to generate DEM simulation cases, execute and monitor simulations, and automatically extract and report physical and process-level metrics. Evaluation across 60 normal-condition cases covering 12 DEM scenarios and parameter variations achieve a simulation success rate of 91.7%. In the error-handling evaluation, all 10 repairable errors are detected and 9 are successfully resolved, while all 5 non-repairable cases are correctly identified and reported. The framework automatically extracts a range of DEM-relevant metrics, including particle size distributions, packing and density measures, velocity profiles, discharge rates, mixing indices, contact force characteristics, and thermal quantities. GranularGPT provides a foundation for improving the accessibility and efficiency of DEM simulation workflows while reducing the specialized expertise required for their operation.

items.title: Hivemind: A Federated Protocol for AI-Mediated Tacit Knowledge Sharing in Organisations
items.abstract: This paper presents Hivemind, a federated protocol that enables AI agents to exchange tacit knowledge on behalf of their users, asynchronously and without requiring any direct human interaction. Individual AI memory systems capture the decisions, reasoning, and contextual knowledge that surface during AI-assisted work. Hivemind creates the shared space in which this captured knowledge can flow between individuals across team and departmental boundaries, addressing a structural gap that neither centralised knowledge repositories nor existing AI tooling closes, even where partial solutions such as expert-finding systems exist. The paper evaluates centralised versus decentralised design approaches, proposes a federated architecture grounded in Nonaka and Takeuchi's (1995) Socialisation, Externalisation, Combination and Internalisation (SECI) model, and demonstrates a proof-of-concept implementation using Design Science Research (DSR) methodology. Measuring the enterprise benefit of federated tacit expertise sharing remains an open task for future work.

items.title: How Developer Personality Shapes the Use of AI Coding Assistants
items.abstract: Developers differ in personality traits that shape how they approach software development tasks, yet AI coding assistants either behave uniformly or offer personalization features whose fit with individual developers must be found through trial and error. This is because it remains unclear how personality shapes developers' experiences with AI assistants, and thus which traits personalization should account for. In other words, we provide tools with no underlying theory on what works when and why. We take a first step towards such a theory with a systematic scoping review on how users' personality relates to their perception of LLM-based tools. We identified twelve studies through general search engines, major Software Engineering (SE) venues, AI tooling, and snowballing. They all reported associations between personality and perceptions, particularly perceived usefulness, yet none addressed this in a SE context. Building on these findings, we conducted an exploratory two-wave survey with 29 and 11 developers, collecting first empirical evidence of how developers' personality (measured using the Big Five Model) relates to the perception of AI coding assistants. Higher Extraversion was associated with more positive private-use experiences in both waves, while Agreeableness was associated with negative professional experiences in the first wave and positive ones in the second. These results provide first indications that the personality effects found in the literature extend to developers. Although further studies with bigger samples are needed to build a theory, our work takes the first step towards an empirical grounded theory of developer personality and AI personalization traits.

items.title: How to Translate Ergonomics Findings into Design-Relevant Principles in an Ergodesign Framework: The Case of Lohr Industrie
items.abstract: Aligning human capabilities with system requirements is crucial for lowering injury risks and enhancing performance in industrial settings like the assembly of automobiles. In this context, we define the Ergodesign Framework as a structure for integrating ergonomics and its findings, Ergodesign and its generation of principles, and design and its pursuit of technical solutions within a transdisciplinary, continuous, and bidirectional process. In this paper, we focus on the internal Ergodesign process, whose objective is to translate ergonomic data into design-relevant principles that can subsequently be applied during design phases, thereby enabling the proactive implementation of ergonomic requirements. The process is based on the capitalization of recurring issues observed during ergonomic analyses, the identification of their root causes, and the definition of Ergodesign rules, making it possible to create a database of Ergodesign principles that can be applied by designers. This process is implemented within the company Lohr Industrie, where standardized elements were developed to define internal rules for product and process design, based on findings from ergonomic studies conducted across different workshops. Through this application, the process of translating ergonomic data into design-relevant principles via Ergodesign emerges as a central component of the Ergodesign Framework.

items.title: Human and Ethical Factors in AI- and IoT-Driven Industry 5.0 Smart Manufacturing: A PRISMA-Guided Systematic and Narrative Review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) are promoted as the technological backbone of Industry 5.0, which re-centres manufacturing on human well-being, resilience, and sustainability. This PRISMA 2020-guided review combines bibliometric analysis with narrative synthesis to examine how the human and ethical dimensions of AI- and IoT-driven smart manufacturing are addressed. Web of Science, Scopus, and IEEE Xplore searches without a start-year limit identified 1904 unique records; all were coded at abstract level (647 eligible records), and 86 prioritized records were synthesized in full text around five research questions: ethical risk, human factors, operationalization of human-centricity, governance, and the technology-readiness gap. Performance, thematic-evolution, co-citation, usage, and readership analyses complement the synthesis. Human-factors and architecture research dominate, yet reviews and conceptual papers prevail, and only 10% of eligible records report industrial validation. Ethical risk is the fastest-growing theme but is operationalized mainly as explainability. Governance is the primary object of 2.8% of eligible records, and its intellectual base is thin: about 3% of these studies cite the EU AI Act, the GDPR, or AI-law scholarship. A human-centric Industry 5.0 maturity model and a research agenda are proposed.

items.title: Human-AI Co-Ideation Across Socio-Technical Configurations: An Interactional Analysis of Planar and Immersive Workspaces
items.abstract: Remote collaborative platforms increasingly integrate generative AI to support group ideation. These platforms are sociotechnical configurations in which spatial mediation, interaction modality, AI output format, and the mechanisms that make contributions visible to a group co-vary as properties of a deployed system. This paper examines how such configurations shape participants' collaboration and their engagement with AI during creative work. We report a comparative study of two commercially available platforms that instantiate contrasting configurations: a planar shared canvas with text-based AI integration, and an immersive virtual reality workspace with concise AI output embedded in the shared space. Fourteen all-women triads completed a structured ideation task consisting of human-only idea generation, AI-supported idea expansion, and group convergence. We analyzed collaboration patterns, selection of AI-generated ideas, perceived idea quality, workload, presence, and their lexical characteristics. The immersive configuration yielded greater spatial presence and introduced a participation paradox, in which spatial freedom enabled exploration and fragmented group coherence; it was also associated with more balanced role distribution during convergence, at the cost of higher physical demand. In both configurations, AI multiplied the idea pool, and ideas groups authored with AI available were rated above participants' own. AI output format: about 21 words per idea on the planar canvas and 3 in the immersive workspace. Tracked how participants evaluated AI-generated ideas and how often they selected them unaltered as finalists. Neither configuration made AI contributions visible or attributable to the group: participants invoked AI individually and asynchronously in both. We derive design implications for AI output format, group-visible AI invocation, and spatial support for convergence

items.title: Human-AI Collaborative Decision Framework for Distributed Aircraft Power Management in Flight Test Operations
items.abstract: During flight test operations, distributed aircraft power systems are typically managed by human operators through centralized monitoring interfaces. Operators must balance system health, mission objectives, and safety margins under dynamically changing test conditions. However, existing systems are largely reactive and primarily provide fault alerts without predictive insight, which can delay timely intervention and increase operator cognitive workload. This paper proposes a human-AI collaborative decision framework for distributed aircraft power management in flight test environments. The framework integrates predictive health assessment, risk modeling, and strategy evaluation to support operator decision making. A lightweight prognostic mechanism continuously estimates the health risk of individual power cabinets using electrical and thermal indicators. Based on the predicted risk, the system identifies high-risk modules and recommends a small set of feasible power management strategies that balance risk mitigation and mission impact. Human operators remain responsible for final decision selection through a human-centered interface that visualizes system health and strategy options. A simulation-based experimental study using a Wizard-of-Oz platform compares conventional manual management with the proposed Human-AI decision support approach. Results show that the framework improves risk detection efficiency, increases decision accuracy, and reduces unnecessary load shedding. The findings demonstrate the potential of human-AI collaboration to enhance situational awareness and decision performance in safety-critical aircraft power management tasks.

items.title: Hybrid-Intelligence Lean Six Sigma for Error-Proof Part Supply: Graph Neural Networks and Multiobjective Optimization
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to eliminate part-supply errors, reduce non-value-added labour, and improve ergonomic conditions in high-mix single-axis linear actuator assembly using the DMAIC methodology. Methods A DMAIC-based case study was conducted in a Vietnamese precision-component manufacturing plant. Pareto analysis, process observation, 4M Ishikawa diagrams, on-site verification, and cause-prioritization matrices identified three root causes from seven candidates. Five improvement solutions were implemented, including single-order kitting, a two-level tray conveyor, centralized automatic ball feeding, point-of-use parts storage, and barcode-based poka-yoke verification. Results Missing and incorrect parts accounted for 76% of assembly part defects, with an initial supply-error rate of 0.31%. Supply errors decreased from 6.33 per month to zero during the post-improvement verification month (p ≈ 0.0018). Ball insertion time decreased by 1.13 minutes per cycle, while non-value-added labour was reduced by 3,203 hours annually. The improvements generated annual savings of US$7,110 from a US$5,200 investment, achieving an 8.8-month payback period and a first-year return on investment of approximately 37%. Value : This study demonstrates a cost-effective, human-centred DMAIC approach integrating error-proofing, material-flow redesign, and ergonomic improvements to enhance assembly quality, operational efficiency, and sustainable manufacturing practices.

items.title: Identifying Barriers and Developing a Roadmap to Adapt a Digital Mental Health Intervention (Wysa) for Adolescent Girls with Anxiety and Depression in Rural Uttar Pradesh, India: Protocol Paper
items.abstract: Background Adolescent girls in rural India face substantial barriers to mental healthcare, including restrictive gender norms, limited digital autonomy and a severe shortage of trained professionals. Digital mental health interventions offer scalable solutions but require contextual adaptation to achieve meaningful engagement. This study aims to identify multi-level barriers and co-produce a stakeholder-endorsed roadmap for adapting the Wysa application, an artificial intelligence-based conversational agent, and its implementation strategies for adolescent girls in rural Uttar Pradesh. It is a formative, pre-implementation intervention-adaptation study and constitutes the first work package of a five-year research programme. Methods and analysis This protocol describes a sequential, participatory mixed-methods study conducted across five districts of Uttar Pradesh, namely Bahraich, Barabanki, Hardoi, Lucknow and Sitapur, with a total sample ranging between 120–175 participants. Step 1 will comprise of 15 in-person participatory workshops with adolescent girls (n = 60–90), parents and guardians (n = 35–50) and community stakeholders (n = 25–35), supplemented by semi-structured interviews with a subset of adolescent girls, analysed thematically and mapped to the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation and Behaviour (COM-B) model and the Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change (ERIC) taxonomy. Step 2 will employ two rounds of Delphi survey (n = 24) to prioritise barriers and candidate strategies against the APEASE criteria. Step 3 will apply a modified nominal group technique (n = 18–24) to co-produce the final adaptation roadmap. Ethics and dissemination The protocol has been approved by the Institutional Review Board of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, Mumbai (2026/51/E26005). Written informed consent, and parental consent with participant assent for minors, will be obtained. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed open-access journals, academic conferences and community-level platforms coordinated with the Lived Experience Advisory Group.
