items.title: Injectra: Retrofitting Extensibility into Web-Based Desktop Applications
items.abstract: Large language models can generate code based on natural language prompts, opening up new possibilities for users to customize software and extend its functionality. This paper proposes and implements Injectra, a general-purpose code injection and feature enhancement system for existing desktop clients, suitable for applications whose user interfaces are built using embedded browser engines (such as Electron) or system WebViews (such as Tauri). Injectra decouples the host integration logic from the upper-layer enhancement code. Combining both runtime integration and pre-launch bootstrap mechanisms, it injects JavaScript, HTML, and CSS into the application's internal Web runtime environment through a unified execution channel, thereby enabling modifications to interface rendering, adjustments to interactive behaviors, and client-side functionality extensions. The system uses a command-line interface (CLI) as a unified entry point, allowing external tools, AI agents, and MCP integration layers to reuse its injection and enhancement capabilities. We tested 38 desktop applications already installed on our macOS machine; code injection was successfully completed for all of them. We demonstrated the system's capability to extend functionality through various enhanced use cases and also successfully validated the Windows version. Based on Injectra, we further developed an LLM-powered enhancement tool driven by selection and annotation: users select interface objects within the original application and describe their modification requirements; the large language model then generates the enhancement code, which is injected, executed, and rendered by Injectra. The system's source code has now been released as open source: https://github.com/sqmw/injectra.

items.title: Integrasi Hadis Niat dan Etika Menuntut Ilmu dalam Pembelajaran PAI Berbasis Project-Based Learning
items.abstract: Digital transformation in Islamic Religious Education (IRE) requires contextual and character-oriented learning innovations. This qualitative library research aims to analyze the takhrij and matn of hadiths regarding intention and the obligation to seek knowledge, and formulates their integration into Project-Based Learning (PjBL). Tracing transmission chains, matn criticism, and pedagogical content analysis were employed. Results show that the hadith on intention (Sahih al-Bukhari No. 1) is authentic (muttafaq 'alaih), serving as an ethical foundation of sincerity, while the hadith on seeking knowledge (Sunan Ibn Majah No. 224) is hasan li ghairihi. Integrating these hadiths into PjBL yields three Islamic academic ethical pillars (al-ikhlas, al-itqan, al-'amal wa al-naf') that enhance students' intrinsic motivation, academic integrity, and social responsibility. This conceptual framework offers an accountable pedagogical innovation for IRE..

items.title: Integrating sustainable technological interventions for cleaner fertilizer production and occupational ammonia exposure reduction
items.abstract: Egypt's fertilizer industry is a major component of the petrochemical sector and relies heavily on ammonia during nitrogenous fertilizer production, creating potential occupational exposure risks for workers. Over the past decade, sustainable technological interventions and pollution-control measures have been implemented to reduce ammonia emissions and improve workplace safety. This study assessed occupational ammonia exposure among workers in a modern nitrogenous fertilizer plant in Alexandria, Egypt, and evaluated the effectiveness of these interventions. Ammonia concentrations were measured at representative operational stations using a MIRAN gas analyzer, and a structured questionnaire was administered to assess workers' occupational characteristics, use of personal protective equipment, health complaints, and awareness of occupational hazards. Ammonia concentrations ranged from 0.70 to 1.06 ppm, remaining approximately 95.8–97.2% below the occupational exposure limit of 25 ppm recommended by the American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH) and the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH). These low exposure levels were completed through the implementation of cleaner production technologies, including the Uhde ammonia synthesis process, replacement of conventional urea melting and prilling with environmentally friendly granulation technology, acidic scrubbing systems, condensate stripping, ammonia recovery and recycling, emission capture systems, and preventive maintenance practices. The findings demonstrate that integrating cleaner production technologies, Best Available Techniques (BAT), continuous environmental monitoring, ammonia detection systems, emergency response measures, and targeted occupational health training can effectively minimize occupational ammonia exposure, enhance worker safety, ensure compliance with international occupational health standards, and promote environmentally sustainable and economically efficient fertilizer production

items.title: Intellectual Tenacity at Work: Generative AI Exposure and the Economic Returns to Occupational Personality Requirements
items.abstract: Technology, including generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), is changing professional work, but its implications for how occupational personality requirements are rewarded in the labor market remain unclear. Using job-incumbent ratings from the U.S. Department of Labor’s Occupational Information Network (O*NET), we identify two personality requirement composites: intellectual tenacity (achievement/effort, persistence, initiative, analytical thinking, innovation, and independence) and social adjustment (emotion regulation, concern for others, social orientation, cooperation, and stress tolerance). We link these measures to more than 15 million workers in the American Community Survey from 2006 to 2024. Intellectual tenacity requirements were positively associated with hourly wages, whereas social adjustment requirements had a weaker, negative association. The wage premium for intellectual tenacity requirements was approximately stable through 2014 and rose thereafter, while the return to social adjustment requirements declined. These divergent trends began before widespread GenAI adoption, but they are concentrated in occupations with greater exposure to GenAI: wage returns for intellectual tenacity requirements increased in occupations highly exposed to GenAI, while returns to social adjustment requirements decreased in those occupations. These findings suggest that broad measures of personality or non-cognitive occupational requirements can obscure opposing shifts in the labor-market value of persistent analytical effort and social adjustment.
